IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r5.claim: Loss means deficiency; the believers who believe, do good, and counsel truth and patience are not diminished.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r5.anchor: والخسر: النقصان إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

BURHAN:v2p232/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p232/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p232/r1.claim: A singular address such as “O human” can address all people; the exception “except those who believe” confirms the universal sense of al-insān in 103:2.
BURHAN:v2p232/r1.anchor: والمراد الجميع بدليل قوله ﴿ إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا ﴾

QASHANI:103:1-3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:103:1-3/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:103:1-3/r1.claim: Affliction falls first on prophets, then saints, then the best people in descending order of spiritual excellence.
QASHANI:103:1-3/r1.anchor: البلاء موكل بالأنبياء ثم الأولياء ثم الأمثل فالأمثل

QASHANI:103:1-3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:103:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:103:1-3/r2.claim: Affliction is God’s whip, by which He drives His servants toward Himself.
QASHANI:103:1-3/r2.anchor: البلاء سوط من سياط الله يسوق به عباده إليه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r2.claim: This sūrah explains life’s real value and the factors that make it a path to salvation or a cause of eternal punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p433/r2.anchor: the real value and importance of life is divulged

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r2.claim: The sūrah briefly lays out the way to use life well and thereby fulfill the individual and collective duties on which salvation depends.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r3.claim: The Qur’an’s guidance to organize personal and collective life for success in the Hereafter is condensed into these three verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r3.anchor: the message which is conveyed by one hundred and fourteen sūrahs of the Qur’ ān has been succinctly put forth in three verses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r4.speaker: Im ām Sh āfi‘ ī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r4.claim: Imām Shāfiʿī is reported to say that reflective reading of Sūrah al-ʿAṣr alone would suffice for people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p434/r4.anchor: Im ām Sh āfi‘ ī has pointed by saying that if people only read S ūrah al-‘A ṣr while reflecting on its contents, it will suffice for them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r1.claim: Faith and righteous action fulfill life’s purpose: defying Satan brings mutual pleasure with God and Paradise, while surrendering to Satan’s lures forfeits an extraordinary favor.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p438/r1.anchor: the Almighty will be pleased with him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r2.claim: Since human beings naturally live in families and society and receive material and moral support there, they must care for others’ welfare rather than remain indifferent.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r2.anchor: by his very nature, he has a gregarious temperament; he is always a part of a family and member of a society

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r3.claim: Believers must urge one another toward truth and patience: ḥaqq includes faith as God’s greatest right and righteous acts concerning God and other people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r3.anchor: īmān is included to the utmost in al-ḥaqq because it is the right of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r4.claim: Patience is needed both to remain steadfast in truth and to call other people toward it; believers therefore counsel one another to persevere in these duties.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p440/r4.anchor: without adhering to perseverance and patience

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r1.claim: The commentary defines ḥaqq as what exists and endures, then gives three common senses: certainty, what reason acknowledges as true, and moral obligation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r1.anchor: The word ḥaqq is used primarily for what exists and continues to exist.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r2.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r2.claim: Farāhī derives the special sense of helping the poor from ḥaqq’s general sense: aid is a right incumbent on the capable, and iḥsān is recognized as maʿrūf.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r2.anchor: After citing various arguments from the Qur’ ān in favour of these three meanings, Im ām Far āhī writes:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r3.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r3.claim: Farāhī says Arab patience means resolve and tenacity, not helpless weakness, and cites Ḥātim Ṭāʾī’s poetry as evidence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r3.anchor: Whilst presenting his research on the word ṣabr , Im ām Far āhī writes:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r4.claim: Ḥātim Ṭāʾī’s cited poem uses language of endurance through severe trials, illustrating patience as fortitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p441/r4.anchor: wa ghamratu mawti ṇ laysa f īhā haw ādatu ṇ

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r1.claim: The Qur’anic example of patience in adversity, illness, and war identifies these as the chief sources of hardship.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r2.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r2.claim: Farāhī says ḥaqq opens the way to virtue, while ṣabr blocks evil; ḥaqq is the desired good and ṣabr the drive to attain it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r2.anchor: A summary of all these details is that ḥaqq opens the door to all virtues and ṣabr closes the door to all evils

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r3.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r3.claim: Farāhī says ḥaqq and ṣabr comprehensively combine virtues and good deeds, with steadfastness sustaining a virtue after it is attained.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r3.anchor: the real thing is steadfastness once a virtue is attained

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r4.claim: Faith is presented as the foundation and nucleus, with righteous deeds following as its explanation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p442/r4.anchor: many branches sprout from a root

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p443/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p443/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p443/r1.claim: Love of ḥaqq produces patience: honor and resolve rise with the value of what is loved, so people defend it and God’s cherished right provokes His anger when damaged.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p443/r1.anchor: The reason for the Almighty’s anger and fury is also because He holds ḥaqq dear

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p443/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p443/r2.speaker: Im ām Far āhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p443/r2.claim: Farāhī says believers who embody ḥaqq and ṣabr also urge others toward them; preaching is implicit in their faith and works, and urging without practice would be ineffective.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p443/r2.anchor: Im ām Far āhī writes in this regard: It is evident from the last part of this third verse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r1.claim: The argument moves from faith to righteous deeds, then from righteous deeds to mutual exhortation toward truth and patience; this exhortation explains righteous deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r1.anchor: urging others towards ḥaqq and ṣabr as actually a part and an explanation of righteous deeds

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r2.claim: A person who cherishes truth is ready to bear hardship to protect it, and wants others to share that love and defend truth when it is oppressed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r2.anchor: would always be ready to bear difficulties and hardships for it s protection

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r3.claim: Urging others to defend truth is a natural expression of the dignity and honour a person feels for truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p444/r3.anchor: would motivate others to defend and protect ḥaqq

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r3.claim: Hasan says the truth people should urge one another toward is God's Book, and patience is obedience to God.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p394/r3.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ وتواصوا بالحق وتواصوا بالصبر ﴾ قال الحق كتاب الله والصبر طاعة الله

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r9.claim: The believers who are excepted worship sincerely and urge one another to truth, what is good and beautiful, and patience.
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r9.anchor: الذين أخلصوا في العبادة وتواصوا بما هو حق

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r10.speaker: بعض التفاسير
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r10.claim: One exegetical mapping identifies the believers with Abū Bakr, good works with ʿUmar, enjoining truth with ʿUthmān, and enjoining patience with ʿAlī.
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r10.anchor: وفي بعض التفاسير : قوله : { الذين آمنوا } يعني أبا بكر ، { وعملوا الصالحات } : يعني عمر

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r14.claim: Enjoining truth means preferring others in dealings with people and being sincere with God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r14.anchor: وهو الإيثار مع الخلق ، والصدق مع الحق

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r15.claim: Patience means enduring well-being, which is the fullest form of patience.

QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r16.claim: Another interpretation is patience with God, which is among the most difficult forms of patience.
QUSHAYRI:v3p446/r16.anchor: ويقال : بالصبر مع الله . . وهو أشد أقسام الصبر

SULAMI:v2p419#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p419#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p419#2/r2.claim: Those exempted are people who fulfill the rights required of them in all acts of worship.
SULAMI:v2p419#2/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : إلا الذين أدوا الحقوق التي لزمتهم في جميع العبادات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الزبير والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn al-Zubayr, and most authorities say the surah is Meccan; Mujāhid, Qatada, and Muqātil say Madinan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول ابن عباس وابن الزبير والجمهور، ومدنية في قول مجاهد وقتادة ومقاتل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r2.claim: After the previous warning against rivalry and repeated threat, this surah distinguishes the state of believer from unbeliever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r2.anchor: لما قال فيما قبلها: ألهاكم التكاثر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that the afternoon prayer is hard to maintain when people are busy with trade and end-of-day accounts; Salam also reads al-ʿaṣr and al-ṣabr with kasra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r7.anchor: لأن التنكيف في أدائها أشق لتهافت الناس في تجاراتهم وتحاسبهم آخر النهار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the kasra readings occur only at pause through transferred vowel; Abu ʿAmr reports and other grammarians describe related pause or movement readings, supported by poetic examples.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p538/r8.anchor: وقرأ سلام: والعصر بكسر الصاد، والصبر بكسر الباء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r1.speaker: الراجز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r1.claim: A rajaz verse ending with fī al-ʿaṣr is cited to show the transferred vowel as evidence for the reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r1.anchor: أنا جرير كنيتي أبو عمر ... أضرب بالسيف وسعد في العصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r3.claim: Trading the afterlife for worldly life is utter loss, whereas the believer buys the afterlife with worldly life and gains; mutual counsel is to follow established truth and persevere in obedience and against sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r3.anchor: ومن باع آخرته بدنياه فهو في غاية الخسران، بخلاف المؤمن، فإنه اشترى الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r5.claim: Al-ḥaqq is the established truth that those who practice it urge one another to follow; ṣabr is perseverance in God's obedience and avoidance of disobedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p539/r5.anchor: وتواصوا بالحق: أي بالأمر الثابت من الذين عملوا به وتواصوا به،

MAJAZ:v2p310/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p310/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p310/r2.claim: Al-insān is singular in wording but collective in meaning, allowing all people to be excepted; ordinarily one would except a singular from a plural.
MAJAZ:v2p310/r2.anchor: «إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات» (2- 3) مجاز «إن الإنسان» فى موضع «إن الأناسى» لأنه يستثنى الجميع من الواحد

MAJAZ:v2p310/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p310/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p310/r3.claim: The same singular-for-collective construction occurs in Qur'an 70:19–22, where al-insān is followed by an exception for worshippers.
MAJAZ:v2p310/r3.anchor: وفى آية أخرى «إن الإنسان خلق هلوعا إذا مسه الشر جزوعا [وإذا مسه الخير منوعا] إلا المصلين» (70/ 19- 22)

MAJAZ:v2p310/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p310/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p310/r4.claim: The singular wording has collective meaning; Qur'an 69:47 likewise has singular aḥad followed by plural ḥājizīn.
MAJAZ:v2p310/r4.anchor: يقع معناه على الجميع وعلى الواحد فى القرآن «فما منكم من أحد عنه حاجزين» (69/ 47)

MAJAZ:v2p310/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p310/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p310/r5.claim: Al-Nābighah's poem illustrates generic singular wording followed by an exception.
MAJAZ:v2p310/r5.anchor: عيت جوابا وما بالربع من أ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r10.claim: Those who believe and do good are exempt from loss.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r11.claim: Tawaasaw means that they counsel one another.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r12.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r12.claim: Hasan and Qatada say that advising one another in truth means advising one another by the Qur'an.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r13.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r13.claim: Maqatil says truth here means faith and God's oneness.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r14.claim: Patience means enduring in performing the obligations and upholding God's command.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r14.anchor: وتواصوا بالصبر} على أداء الفرائض وإقامة أمر الله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r15.speaker: إبراهيم عن ابن عون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r15.claim: Ibrahim, transmitted by Ibn Awn, says aging and infirmity bring decline, except for believers whose youthful, healthy deeds continue to be recorded; this parallels 95:4–6.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p522#2/r15.anchor: وروى ابن عون عن إبراهيم قال: أراد أن الإنسان إذا عمر في الدنيا وهرم،

BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r3.claim: Believers who act righteously trade worldly life for the eternal afterlife; counsel one another in true belief and action, and patience from sins, for truth, or through trials.
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r3.anchor: { إلا الذين ءامنوا وعملوا الصلحت } فإنهم اشتروا الآخرة بالدنيا ففازوا بالحياة الأبدية

BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r4.claim: Counseling patience is a specific case after general good works, unless good works means acts performed perfectly; only profit’s causes are named to imply omitted pursuits lose, or graciously leave loss vague.
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r4.anchor: وهذا من عطف الخاص على العام للمبالغة إلا أن يخص العمل بما يكون مقصورا

BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r5.claim: A report promises forgiveness and inclusion among those counseling truth and patience to whoever recites Sūrat al-ʿAṣr; no grading is stated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:103:1-3/r5.anchor: من قرأ سورة والعصر غفر الله له وكان ممن تواصوا بالحق وتواصوا بالصبر

BINTSHATI:v2p93/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p93/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p93/r1.claim: Surah al-Asr and al-Balad establish social responsibility, especially enjoining right and forbidding wrong, as a foundation of religion and a means of avoiding loss.
BINTSHATI:v2p93/r1.anchor: فبمثل هذا التقرير الحاسم في سورتى العصر والبلد، تتقرر مسئولية الإنسان الاجتماعية

BINTSHATI:v2p93/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p93/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p93/r2.claim: The Quran condemns Israelites who failed to forbid wrongdoing and hypocrites who commanded evil and withheld good.
BINTSHATI:v2p93/r2.anchor: كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون

BINTSHATI:v2p93/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p93/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p93/r3.claim: The author argues that no secular law can raise people to Islam's level of social responsibility, which grounds goodness and faith and protects from ruin.
BINTSHATI:v2p93/r3.anchor: هيهات لشريعة وضعية أن ترقى بالإنسان إلى مثل هذا المستوى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r4.speaker: الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r4.claim: Al-Ghazālī likens the Qur'an to a sea containing six minerals: knowledge of God, His attributes and acts, the afterlife, worship, doubts that harm faith, and lessons from the saved and ruined.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r4.anchor: على ما قال الغزالي : إن القرآن كالبحر الذي فيه جزائر بها معادن ستة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r6.claim: The surah's other clauses map to knowledge of God and the afterlife, required and preparatory worship, and patience that completes the effort to avoid doubt and harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r6.anchor: والخامسة وسيلة إليها ومتمة لها لأن معرفة ذلك واجتنابه لا يكون إلا ببذل الجهد في الصبر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r7.claim: The basmala says all things perish except God, whose mercy reaches everyone and whose completed gifts distinguish His chosen allies.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521/r7.anchor: بسم الله } الذي كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه { الرحمن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r4.speaker: الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r4.claim: Al-Ghazālī likens the Qur'an to a sea containing six minerals: knowledge of God, His attributes and acts, the afterlife, worship, doubts that harm faith, and lessons from the saved and ruined.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r4.anchor: على ما قال الغزالي : إن القرآن كالبحر الذي فيه جزائر بها معادن ستة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r6.claim: The surah's other clauses map to knowledge of God and the afterlife, required and preparatory worship, and patience that completes the effort to avoid doubt and harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r6.anchor: والخامسة وسيلة إليها ومتمة لها لأن معرفة ذلك واجتنابه لا يكون إلا ببذل الجهد في الصبر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r7.claim: The basmala says all things perish except God, whose mercy reaches everyone and whose completed gifts distinguish His chosen allies.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p521#s103/r7.anchor: بسم الله } الذي كل شيء هالك إلا وجهه { الرحمن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r4.claim: Faith means affirming what is necessarily known to have been brought by the Prophet: God's oneness, angels, books, messengers, and the Last Day.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r4.anchor: أي أوجدوا الإيمان وهو التصديق بما علم بالضرورة مجيء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم به من توحيده سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r5.claim: The past-tense wording encourages entry into the religion even at its lowest initial degree and promises salvation to whoever fulfills its conditions.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r5.anchor: ولعل حكمة التعبير بالماضي الحث على الدخول في الدين ولو على أدنى الدرجات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r6.claim: Humans are rational animals whose perfection lies in voluntary practical action, rather than being driven by overpowering animal appetite.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r6.anchor: وكان كمال حيوانيته في القوة العملية للحركة بالإرادة لا بمقتضى الشهوة القاسرة البهيمية

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r7.claim: Righteous deeds mean following commands and avoiding prohibitions in worship and ordinary dealings, such as prayer and buying and selling.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r7.anchor: وهو اتبع الأوامر واجتناب النواهي في العبادات كالصلاة والعادات كالبيع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r8.claim: Through righteous deeds, believers become Muslims after being believers, trade the world for the next life, and escape distraction by accumulation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r8.anchor: فكانوا بهذا مسلمين بعد أن كانوا مؤمنين فاشتروا الآخرة بالدنيا فلم يلههم التكاثر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r9.claim: A person cannot escape loss merely by perfecting himself; he must also complete others, since prophets were sent to guide and religion requires communal mutual exhortation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r9.anchor: لا ينتفي عنه مطلق الخسر - إلا بتكميل غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r10.claim: Truth includes everything the sacred law deems correct, whether speech, deed, belief, action, or abstention.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r10.anchor: وهو كل ما حكم الشرع بصحته فلا يصح بوجه نفيه من قول أو عمل أو اعتقاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r11.claim: Mutual counsel is necessary because religion is sustained through enjoining right and forbidding wrong, which arise from an illuminated heart and require community.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r11.anchor: وكان الدين لا يقوم , وإذا قام لا يتم إلا بالأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر الناشئ عن نور القلب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r12.claim: The righteous become beneficent by advising one another in truth and perfecting others through practical virtue.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r12.anchor: فكانوا محسنين , والتكميل في القوة العملية باجتلاب الخيور

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r13.claim: Counsel in patience is needed because the righteous face hostility from the unjust majority and must endure obedience, vindicating truth, resisting wrong, and the resulting harm until death.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r14.claim: Mutual exhortation and patience complete practical perfection while preserving the earlier intellectual perfection; worship aims at Paradise externally and an inward light drawing one near to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r14.anchor: وهي هنا أمران : خارج عن العامل وهو الجنة , وداخل قائم به وهو النور المقرب من الحق سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r15.claim: The wording 'mutually enjoined' signals gentleness in commanding right and forbidding wrong, using soft counsel to the utmost effort.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r15.anchor: واختير التعبير بالوصية إشارة إلى الرفق في الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r16.claim: Patience is the human essence and distillation, attained by disciplining the self into obedience and adherence to the Sunna and community until it becomes habitual.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r16.anchor: والصبر هو خلاصة الإنسان وسره وصفاوته وزبدته وعصارته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r17.claim: He reads the fourteen words as alluding to permission for jihad in the fourteenth prophetic year, the Hijra year, when jihad embodied enjoining right and the truth prevailed at Badr.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p523/r17.anchor: وهي أربع عشرة كلمة تشير إلى أن في اسنة الرابعة عشر من النبوة يكون الإذن في الجهاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r1.claim: At the Confederates, the believers were terrified, as eyes turned and hearts reached their throats.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r1.anchor: وفي الأحزاب زاغت الأبصار وبلغت القلوب الحناجر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r2.claim: He cites 3:173, where those who warned that enemies had assembled against the believers only increased their faith, and they answered that God was sufficient for them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r2.anchor: الذي قال لهم الناس إن الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم فزادهم إيمانا وقالوا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r3.claim: The Prophet said after the Confederates that thereafter the Muslims would campaign against their foes rather than be raided by them.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r3.anchor: أسفرت عاقبة الصبر فيها عما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عند ذهابهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r4.claim: Adding four pronouns to the word count alludes to year nine, the difficult Tabuk expedition, whose patient hardship was followed by arriving delegations and honor for Islam.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p524/r4.anchor: فإذا ضممت إليها الضمائر الأربعة أشارت إلى سنة تسع , وقد كانت فيها غزوة تبوك وهي غزوة العسرة

NAHHAS:v5p286/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p286/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p286/r3.claim: Those who believe form an exception from the general loss, and the relative clause and remaining deeds are coordinated with belief.
NAHHAS:v5p286/r3.anchor: الذين في موضع استثناء من موجب ( آمنوا ) صلته

DURR-FULL:v8p621/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r12.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r12.claim: Qatada says enjoining truth means the Book of God and enjoining patience means obeying God.
DURR-FULL:v8p621/r12.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {والعصر} قال: ساعة من ساعات النهار وفي قوله: {وتواصوا بالحق} قال: كتاب الله {وتواصوا بالصبر} قال: طاعة الله

DURR-FULL:v8p622/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p622/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p622/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Ali and Salman among those who believe and do good.
DURR-FULL:v8p622/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر} يعني أبا جهل بن هشام {إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} ذكر عليا وسلمان

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r2.claim: Qatadah glosses enjoining one another to truth as enjoining God's Book, and enjoining patience as obedience to God.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r2.anchor: وفي قوله : وتوصوا بالحق قال : كتاب الله . وقوله تعالى : وتواصوا بالصبر قال : طاعة الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says all people are in loss; belief alone is not enough, and the verse successively requires good works, mutual counsel in truth, and mutual counsel in patience.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3462/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي والعصر قال : قسم اقسم الله به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r4.claim: Abu Amr's reported kasra on ba in bi-l-sabr is an ishmam reading, likewise limited to pausing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p520#3/r4.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو: «بالصبر» بكسر الباء إشماما، وهذا أيضا لا يكون إلا في الوقف.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r2.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r2.claim: A report says that before accepting Islam, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ told Musaylima that a brief, eloquent sūra had been revealed and recited al-ʿAṣr; Musaylima answered with a parody.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r2.anchor: ذكروا أن عمرو بن العاص وفد على مسيلمة الكذاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r3.claim: Al-Wabr is a small animal resembling a cat, notable for its ears; Musaylima's incoherent imitation failed to impress even an idol-worshipper.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r3.anchor: والوبر: دويبة تشبه الهر، أعظم شيء فيه أذناه، وصدره وباقيه دميم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r4.claim: Al-Kharāʾiṭī also recorded this story, or something close to it, in the second part of his book on bad character.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r4.anchor: وقد رأيت أبا بكر الخرائطي أسند (4) في كتابه المعروف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن حصن أبو مدينة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī reports that two Companions would recite Sūrat al-ʿAṣr to each other whenever they met, then exchange greetings before parting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن حصن [أبي مدينة] ، قال: كان الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r6.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says that if people reflected on this sūra, it would suffice them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p479/r6.anchor: وقال الشافعي، رحمه الله: لو تدبر الناس هذه السورة، لوسعتهم

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r1.speaker: أبي
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet promises that reciting Sūrat al-ʿAṣr brings patience and companionship with the people of truth on the Resurrection Day.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r1.anchor: وعن أبي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (والعصر) ختم الله له بالصبر

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r2.claim: After warning about those distracted by worldly abundance, this chapter says people are in loss unless they do good and avoid disobedience.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r2.anchor: ولما ختم السورة بوعيد من ألهاه التكاثر بالدنيا، افتتح هذه السورة بأن الإنسان في خسر

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r8.claim: Ṣabr is restraining the self from whatever it desires to pursue.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r8.anchor: والصبر: حبس النفس عما تنازع إليه من الأمر

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r11.speaker: ابن علي بن عبد الله بن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r11.claim: A report maps the exception to four figures: Abū Bakr believed, ʿUmar did good deeds, ʿUthmān urged truth, and ʿAlī urged patience; Ubayy ibn Kaʿb transmits it as prophetic, but the author says the exception is general.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r11.anchor: أبو بكر (وعملوا الصالحات) عمر (وتواصوا بالحق) عثمان (وتواصوا بالصبر) علي

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r12.claim: The warning and exception apply generally, as shown by the form of the exception.

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r22.claim: Tawāṣaw bi-l-ḥaqq means they urge others to obey and follow the truth, which includes all God commands; another explanation narrows it to the Qur'an or to faith and divine oneness.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r22.anchor: وتواصوا بالحق يعني أمروا غيرهم بالطاعة والحق، وهو جميع ما أمر الله تعالى به

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r23.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r23.claim: They explain al-ḥaqq as the Qur'an.
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r23.anchor: وقيل: الحق القرآن، عن الحسن وقتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7529/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r24.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7529/r24.claim: He explains al-ḥaqq as faith and God's oneness.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r9.claim: The truth is what is established and cannot rightly be denied, encompassing all good: monotheism, obedience, following revelation and messengers, and preferring the afterlife.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r9.anchor: بالأمر الثابت الذي لا يسوغ إنكاره ، وهو الخير كله : من توحيد الله وطاعته ، واتباع كتبه ورسله ، والزهد في الدنيا ، والرغبة في الآخرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r10.claim: Patience means refraining from sins, persisting in obedience, and enduring the trials with which God tests His servants.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p800/r10.anchor: عن المعاصي وعلى الطاعات ، على ما يبلو الله به عباده

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r12.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r12.claim: Yahya ibn Sallam interprets the truth as God's oneness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r12.anchor: أحدها : أنه التوحيد , قاله يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r13.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r13.claim: Qatada says it means the Qur'an.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r14.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r14.claim: Al-Suddi says the truth is God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r15.claim: Mawardi allows that a person should exhort those left behind at death to die only as Muslims.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r15.anchor: أن يوصي مخلفيه عند حضور المنية ألا يموتن إلا وهم مسلمون

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r16.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r16.claim: Qatada says believers exhort one another to patience in obeying God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r16.anchor: أحدهما : على طاعة الله , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r17.speaker: هشام بن حسان
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r17.claim: Hisham ibn Hassan says the exhortation is to fulfill what God has prescribed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r17.anchor: الثاني : على ما افترض الله , قاله هشام بن حسان .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p333#2/r18.claim: Mawardi also allows patience in resisting forbidden acts and following desires.

MUQATIL:103:1-3/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r5.claim: Those excepted—people who believe and do righteous deeds—are not in loss.
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r5.anchor: { إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات } فليسوا في خسران

MUQATIL:103:1-3/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r6.claim: Counseling one another in truth means affirming God's oneness; counseling one another in patience means perseverance in God's command.
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r6.anchor: { وتواصوا بالحق } يعني بتوحيد الله عز وجل { وتواصوا بالصبر } [آية: 3] يعني على أمر الله عز وجل

MUQATIL:103:1-3/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r7.claim: Whoever does these things belongs among the believers and righteous, escapes loss, and remains forever in the Gardens.
MUQATIL:103:1-3/r7.anchor: فمن فعل هذين كان من الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات، فليسوا من الخسران في شىء، ولكنهم في الجنان مخلدون

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan, has three verses, and compresses Islam's full way of life and the Muslim community's identity and role into a brief constitution.

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r2.claim: The surah presents the Muslim community's essence and function in its final verse, a concise form of inimitable divine expression.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r2.anchor: وتصف الأمة المسلمة : حقيقتها ووظيفتها . في آية واحدة هي الآية الثالثة من السورة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r3.claim: Across all ages there is one successful path: faith, righteous action, and mutual exhortation to truth and patience; every other way ends in loss.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r3.anchor: ليس هنالك إلا منهج واحد رابح ، وطريق واحد ناج . هو ذلك المنهج الذي ترسم السورة حدوده

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r4.claim: Qutb discusses faith's nature and value in life rather than defining it in juristic terms.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r4.anchor: نحن لا نعرف الإيمان هنا تعريفه الفقهي ؛ ولكننا نتحدث عن طبيعته وقيمته في الحياة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r5.claim: Faith joins finite humanity to the eternal source of existence, the cosmos and its laws, and powers beyond the individual's limits.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r5.anchor: إنه اتصال هذا الكائن الإنساني الفاني الصغير المحدود بالأصل المطلق الأزلي الباقي الذي صدر عنه الوجود

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r6.claim: This connection gives life beauty, companionship with creation, spiritual joy, and a gain whose loss has no equal.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r6.anchor: فإذا الحياة رحلة في مهرجان إلهي مقام للبشر في كل مكان وفي كل أوان

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r7.claim: Worship of one God frees people from servitude to others and grounds their equality and true liberation.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r7.anchor: التعبد لإله واحد ، يرفع الإنسان عن العبودية لسواه ، ويقيم في نفسه المساواة مع جميع العباد

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r8.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r8.claim: Divine orientation makes God the source of values, laws, and standards, displacing caprice and self-interest with justice and revealed law.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r8.anchor: والربانية التي تحدد الجهة التي يتلقى منها الإنسان تصوراته وقيمه وموازينه واعتباراته وشرائعه وقوانينه

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r9.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r9.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r9.claim: A direct, clear relation between Creator and creature gives the heart light and peace and removes fear, anxiety, and unjust arrogance.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r9.anchor: ووضوح الصلة بين الخالق والمخلوق ، وتبين مقام الألوهية ومقام العبودية على حقيقتهما الناصعة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r10.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r10.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r10.claim: Steadfastness on God's method makes good deliberate, continuous, cooperative, and transmitted across generations in a unified community.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r10.anchor: والاستقامة على المنهج الذي يريده الله . فلا يكون الخير فلتة عارضة ، ولا نزوة طارئة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r11.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r11.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r11.claim: Belief in human dignity before God raises self-respect and awakens shame at falling below the rank God bestowed.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r11.anchor: والاعتقاد بكرامة الإنسان على الله ، يرفع من اعتباره في نظر نفسه ، ويثير في ضميره الحياء

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r12.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r12.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r12.claim: Qutb condemns Darwinian, Freudian, and Marxist influences for portraying degradation as natural and therefore nothing to be ashamed of.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r12.anchor: كانت إيحاءات الدارونية والفرويدية والماركسية هي أبشع ما تبتلى به الفطرة البشرية

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r13.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r13.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r13.claim: Human moral cleanliness follows from dignity before God and awareness that God watches inner thoughts and secret feelings.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r13.anchor: ونظافة المشاعر تجيء نتيجة مباشرة للشعور بكرامة الإنسان على الله . ثم برقابة الله على الضمائر

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r14.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r14.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r14.claim: Moral awareness naturally follows belief in a just, merciful, forgiving God who loves good and knows hidden thoughts.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r14.anchor: والحاسة الأخلاقية ثمرة طبيعية وحتمية للإيمان بإله عادل رحيم عفو كريم ودود حليم

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r15.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r15.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r15.claim: Free choice under God's comprehensive oversight creates alertness and responsibility to oneself, society, goodness, and all humanity.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r15.anchor: وهناك التبعة المترتبة على حرية الإرادة وشمول الرقابة ، وما تثيره في حس المؤمن من يقظة وحساسية

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r16.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r16.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r16.claim: Faith loosens attachment to worldly gain and impatience for results; seeking God's reward sustains good despite delayed outcomes and strengthens resistance to evil.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r16.anchor: والارتفاع عن التكالب على أعراض الحياة الدنيا - وهو بعض إيحاءات الإيمان - واختيار ما عند الله

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r17.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r17.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r17.claim: Faith is the root and organizing axis of goodness; detached deeds become lifeless, scattered, or satanic and lack lasting direction.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r17.anchor: إن الإيمان هو أصل الحياة الكبير ، الذي ينبثق منه كل فرع من فروع الخير

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r18.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r18.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r18.claim: The Qur'an nullifies the value of deeds disconnected from faith, comparing them to windblown ash and a mirage.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r18.anchor: ومن ثم يهدر القرآن قيمة كل عمل لا يرجع إلى هذا الأصل ، ولا يشد إلى هذا المحور

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r19.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r19.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r19.claim: Faith shows that human nature is sound and in harmony with the cosmos; failure to respond to the universe's signs indicates a defect that invalidates apparently good deeds.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r19.anchor: إن الإيمان دليل على صحة الفطرة وسلامة التكوين الإنساني ، وتناسقه مع فطرة الكون كله

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r20.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r20.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r20.claim: The believer's world is broad, elevated, beautiful, and joyful, while unbelief leaves people in a diminished and miserable condition.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r20.anchor: وإن عالم المؤمن من السعة والشمول والامتداد والارتفاع والجمال والسعادة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r21.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r21.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r21.claim: Righteous action is faith's natural fruit and begins as soon as faith settles in the heart.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r21.anchor: والعمل الصالح وهو الثمرة الطبيعية للإيمان ، والحركة الذاتية التي تبدأ في ذات اللحظة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r22.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r22.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r22.claim: Islamic faith cannot remain dormant: if it does not appear as outward righteous action, it is false or dead.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r22.anchor: فالإيمان حقيقة إيجابية متحركة . ما أن تستقر في الضمير حتى تسعى بذاتها إلى تحقيق ذاتها

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r23.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r23.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r23.claim: Faith is constructive movement and building, not withdrawal or good intentions that never take form in action.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r23.anchor: ومن هنا قيمة الإيمان . . إنه حركة وعمل وبناء وتعمير . . يتجه إلى الله

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r24.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r24.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r24.claim: Because God's method is purposeful, continuous movement, believing leadership guides humanity into constructive movement in the world.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r24.anchor: وهذا المنهج حركة دائمة متصلة في صميم الوجود . صادرة عن تدبير ، متجهة إلى غاية

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r25.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r25.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r25.claim: Mutual exhortation reveals a Muslim community with a distinct identity, bond, and shared direction, responsible for guiding humanity and carrying a great trust.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r25.anchor: أما التواصي بالحق والتواصي بالصبر فتبرز من خلالها صورة الأمة المسلمة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r26.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r26.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r26.claim: The word tawāṣī evokes an affectionate, cooperative, and mutually supportive community guarding truth and justice.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r26.anchor: متواصية بالحق والصبر في مودة وتعاون وتآخ تنضح بها كلمة التواصي في القرآن

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r27.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r27.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r27.claim: Truth is hard to uphold against ego, self-interest, social norms, tyrants, and oppression; mutual exhortation supplies reminders, courage, and solidarity.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r27.anchor: والتواصي بالحق ضرورة . فالنهوض بالحق عسير . والمعوقات عن الحق كثيرة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r28.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r28.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r28.claim: Patience is necessary in striving against oneself and others, enduring harm and hardship, brazen falsehood, slow progress, obscured signs, and a distant end.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r28.anchor: والتواصي بالصبر كذلك ضرورة . فالقيام على الإيمان والعمل الصالح ، وحراسة الحق والعدل

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r29.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r29.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r29.claim: Mutual exhortation to patience increases capacity through shared purpose, solidarity, love, resolve, and the communal conditions in which Islam is lived.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r29.anchor: والتواصي بالصبر يضاعف المقدرة ، بما يبعثه من إحساس بوحدة الهدف ، ووحدة المتجه

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r30.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r30.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r30.claim: Qutb sees worldly loss spreading because humanity turns away from God's good and lacks righteous authority; he says Muslims who claim Islam have strayed furthest from its guidance.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r30.anchor: يهولنا أن نرى الخسر يحيق بالبشرية في كل مكان على ظهر الأرض بلا استثناء

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r31.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r31.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r31.claim: The Arab lands that first received Islam abandoned its God-given banner for nationalist banners, although Islam had enabled Arabs to lead humanity righteously.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r31.anchor: البقاع التي انبعث منها هذا الخير أول مرة تترك الراية التي رفعها لها الله ، راية الإيمان

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r32.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r32.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r32.claim: Al-Nadwi presents the rise of Muslim leadership as an exceptionally righteous and beneficial chapter in human history.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r32.anchor: يقول الأستاذ أبو الحسن الندوي في كتابه القيم

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r33.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r33.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r33.claim: Al-Nadwi says Muslim leaders governed through revealed scripture and divine law rather than self-made legislation, with divine guidance for just rule.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r33.anchor: أولا : أنهم أصحاب كتاب منزل وشريعة إلهية ، فلا يقننون ولا يشترعون من عند أنفسهم

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r34.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r34.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r34.claim: Al-Nadwi says Muslim leaders received long moral and spiritual training under Muhammad before taking power, cultivating piety, honesty, selflessness, and fear of God.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r34.anchor: مكثوا زمنا طويلا تحت تربية محمد [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] وإشرافه الدقيق

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r35.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r35.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r35.claim: Al-Nadwi cites the rule that leadership should not be entrusted to a person who asks for office or eagerly seeks it.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r35.anchor: إنا والله لا نولي هذا العمل أحدا سأله ، أو أحدا حرص عليه

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r36.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r36.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r36.claim: Al-Nadwi says office was treated as a trust and divine test, with leaders accountable for justice and every matter entrusted to them.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r36.anchor: بل عدوه أمانة في عنقهم ، وامتحانا من الله

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r37.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r37.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r37.claim: Al-Nadwi rejects ethnic or national imperialism as the Muslim mission: its aim was to free all people from serving humans and direct them to God.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r37.anchor: ثالثا : أنهم لم يكونوا خدمة جنس ، ورسل شعب أو وطن

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r38.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r38.speaker: ربعي بن عامر
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r38.claim: At Yazdegerd's court, Rib'i ibn Amir described the Muslim mission as freeing people from human servitude, worldly confinement, and religious injustice.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r38.anchor: كما قال ربعي بن عامر رسول المسلمين في مجلس يزدجرد : الله ابتعثنا لنخرج الناس من عبادة العباد إلى عبادة الله وحده

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r39.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r39.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r39.claim: Al-Nadwi says all peoples are equal and honor rests in piety rather than ancestry, in keeping with the Qur'anic call to know one another.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r39.anchor: فالأمم عندهم سواء ، والناس عندهم سواء . الناس كلهم من آدم ، وآدم من تراب

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r40.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r40.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r40.claim: Qutb recounts Umar's order that an Egyptian whom the governor's son had struck receive redress, affirming that people are born free.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r40.anchor: وقد قال عمر بن الخطاب لعمرو بن العاص عامل مصر - وقد ضرب ابنه مصريا

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r41.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r41.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r41.claim: Al-Nadwi says Muslim rule shared religious learning, education, and government across peoples; many non-Arabs excelled and became leading scholars.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r41.anchor: في ظل هؤلاء وتحت حكمهم استطاعت الأمم والشعوب - حتى المضطهدة منها في القديم - أن تنال نصيبها من الدين والعلم

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r42.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r42.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r42.claim: Al-Nadwi argues that a sound civilization must nourish the whole person—body, spirit, heart, reason, emotions, and limbs—in balanced proportion.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r42.anchor: إن الإنسان جسم وروح ، وهو ذو قلب وعقل وعواطف وجوارح

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r43.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r43.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r43.claim: Al-Nadwi presents the Rightly Guided Caliphate as an ideal civilization joining spiritual, moral, religious, scientific, and material strengths, with strong social relations and relatively little crime.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r43.anchor: فلم نعرف دورا من أدوار التاريخ أكمل وأجمل وأزهر في جميع هذه النواحي من هذا الدور - دور الخلافة الراشدة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r44.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r44.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r44.claim: Earthly profit and loss are small beside the lasting stakes of Paradise and God's pleasure; the final loss is the collapse of human dignity.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r44.anchor: هناك الربح والخسر : ربح الجنة والرضوان ، أو خسر الجنة والرضوان

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r45.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r45.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r45.claim: The surah decisively sets one route out of loss: faith, righteous work, and a community that mutually guards truth with patience.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r45.anchor: طريق واحد لا يتعدد . طريق الإيمان والعمل الصالح وقيام الجماعة المسلمة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r46.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r46.speaker: الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r46.claim: Qutb reports that two Companions would not part after meeting until one recited Surat al-Asr to the other, renewing their commitment to its guidance.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:1/r46.anchor: كان الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] إذا التقيا لم يتفرقا حتى يقرأ أحدهما على الآخر سورة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r1.claim: Qutb treats mutual exhortation to truth and patience as defining the Muslim community's distinct identity and bond.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r1.anchor: أما التواصي بالحق والتواصي بالصبر فتبرز من خلالها صورة الأمة المسلمة - أو الجماعة المسلمة - ذات الكيان الخاص

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r2.claim: Across all ages there is one successful path: faith, righteous action, and mutual exhortation to truth and patience; every other way ends in loss.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r2.anchor: طريق واحد لا يتعدد . طريق الإيمان والعمل الصالح وقيام الجماعة المسلمة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r3.claim: Qutb discusses faith's nature and value in life rather than defining it in juristic terms.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r3.anchor: نحن لا نعرف الإيمان هنا تعريفه الفقهي ؛ ولكننا نتحدث عن طبيعته وقيمته في الحياة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r4.claim: Faith joins finite humanity to the eternal source of existence, the cosmos and its laws, and powers beyond the individual's limits.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r4.anchor: إنه اتصال هذا الكائن الإنساني الفاني الصغير المحدود بالأصل المطلق الأزلي الباقي الذي صدر عنه الوجود

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r5.claim: This connection gives life beauty, companionship with creation, spiritual joy, and a gain whose loss has no equal.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r5.anchor: فإذا الحياة رحلة في مهرجان إلهي مقام للبشر في كل مكان وفي كل أوان

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r6.claim: Worship of one God frees people from servitude to others and grounds their equality and true liberation.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r6.anchor: التعبد لإله واحد ، يرفع الإنسان عن العبودية لسواه ، ويقيم في نفسه المساواة مع جميع العباد

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r7.claim: Divine orientation makes God the source of values, laws, and standards, displacing caprice and self-interest with justice and revealed law.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r7.anchor: والربانية التي تحدد الجهة التي يتلقى منها الإنسان تصوراته وقيمه وموازينه واعتباراته وشرائعه وقوانينه

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r8.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r8.claim: A direct, clear relation between Creator and creature gives the heart light and peace and removes fear, anxiety, and unjust arrogance.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r8.anchor: ووضوح الصلة بين الخالق والمخلوق ، وتبين مقام الألوهية ومقام العبودية على حقيقتهما الناصعة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r9.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r9.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r9.claim: Steadfastness on God's method makes good deliberate, continuous, cooperative, and transmitted across generations in a unified community.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r9.anchor: والاستقامة على المنهج الذي يريده الله . فلا يكون الخير فلتة عارضة ، ولا نزوة طارئة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r10.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r10.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r10.claim: Belief in human dignity before God raises self-respect and awakens shame at falling below the rank God bestowed.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r10.anchor: والاعتقاد بكرامة الإنسان على الله ، يرفع من اعتباره في نظر نفسه ، ويثير في ضميره الحياء

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r11.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r11.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r11.claim: Qutb condemns Darwinian, Freudian, and Marxist influences for portraying degradation as natural and therefore nothing to be ashamed of.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r11.anchor: كانت إيحاءات الدارونية والفرويدية والماركسية هي أبشع ما تبتلى به الفطرة البشرية

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r12.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r12.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r12.claim: Human moral cleanliness follows from dignity before God and awareness that God watches inner thoughts and secret feelings.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r12.anchor: ونظافة المشاعر تجيء نتيجة مباشرة للشعور بكرامة الإنسان على الله . ثم برقابة الله على الضمائر

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r13.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r13.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r13.claim: Moral awareness naturally follows belief in a just, merciful, forgiving God who loves good and knows hidden thoughts.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r13.anchor: والحاسة الأخلاقية ثمرة طبيعية وحتمية للإيمان بإله عادل رحيم عفو كريم ودود حليم

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r14.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r14.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r14.claim: Free choice under God's comprehensive oversight creates alertness and responsibility to oneself, society, goodness, and all humanity.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r14.anchor: وهناك التبعة المترتبة على حرية الإرادة وشمول الرقابة ، وما تثيره في حس المؤمن من يقظة وحساسية

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r15.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r15.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r15.claim: Faith loosens attachment to worldly gain and impatience for results; seeking God's reward sustains good despite delayed outcomes and strengthens resistance to evil.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r15.anchor: والارتفاع عن التكالب على أعراض الحياة الدنيا - وهو بعض إيحاءات الإيمان - واختيار ما عند الله

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r16.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r16.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r16.claim: Faith is the root and organizing axis of goodness; detached deeds become lifeless, scattered, or satanic and lack lasting direction.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r16.anchor: إن الإيمان هو أصل الحياة الكبير ، الذي ينبثق منه كل فرع من فروع الخير

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r17.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r17.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r17.claim: The Qur'an nullifies the value of deeds disconnected from faith, comparing them to windblown ash and a mirage.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r17.anchor: ومن ثم يهدر القرآن قيمة كل عمل لا يرجع إلى هذا الأصل ، ولا يشد إلى هذا المحور

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r18.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r18.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r18.claim: Faith shows that human nature is sound and in harmony with the cosmos; failure to respond to the universe's signs indicates a defect that invalidates apparently good deeds.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r18.anchor: إن الإيمان دليل على صحة الفطرة وسلامة التكوين الإنساني ، وتناسقه مع فطرة الكون كله

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r19.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r19.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r19.claim: The believer's world is broad, elevated, beautiful, and joyful, while unbelief leaves people in a diminished and miserable condition.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r19.anchor: وإن عالم المؤمن من السعة والشمول والامتداد والارتفاع والجمال والسعادة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r20.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r20.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r20.claim: Righteous action is faith's natural fruit and begins as soon as faith settles in the heart.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r20.anchor: والعمل الصالح وهو الثمرة الطبيعية للإيمان ، والحركة الذاتية التي تبدأ في ذات اللحظة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r21.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r21.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r21.claim: Islamic faith cannot remain dormant: if it does not appear as outward righteous action, it is false or dead.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r21.anchor: فالإيمان حقيقة إيجابية متحركة . ما أن تستقر في الضمير حتى تسعى بذاتها إلى تحقيق ذاتها

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r22.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r22.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r22.claim: Faith is constructive movement and building, not withdrawal or good intentions that never take form in action.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r22.anchor: ومن هنا قيمة الإيمان . . إنه حركة وعمل وبناء وتعمير . . يتجه إلى الله

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r23.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r23.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r23.claim: Because God's method is purposeful, continuous movement, believing leadership guides humanity into constructive movement in the world.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r23.anchor: وهذا المنهج حركة دائمة متصلة في صميم الوجود . صادرة عن تدبير ، متجهة إلى غاية

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r24.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r24.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r24.claim: Mutual exhortation reveals a Muslim community with a distinct identity, bond, and shared direction, responsible for guiding humanity and carrying a great trust.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r24.anchor: أما التواصي بالحق والتواصي بالصبر فتبرز من خلالها صورة الأمة المسلمة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r25.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r25.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r25.claim: The word tawāṣī evokes an affectionate, cooperative, and mutually supportive community guarding truth and justice.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r25.anchor: متواصية بالحق والصبر في مودة وتعاون وتآخ تنضح بها كلمة التواصي في القرآن

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r26.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r26.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r26.claim: Truth is hard to uphold against ego, self-interest, social norms, tyrants, and oppression; mutual exhortation supplies reminders, courage, and solidarity.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r26.anchor: والتواصي بالحق ضرورة . فالنهوض بالحق عسير . والمعوقات عن الحق كثيرة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r27.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r27.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r27.claim: Patience is necessary in striving against oneself and others, enduring harm and hardship, brazen falsehood, slow progress, obscured signs, and a distant end.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r27.anchor: والتواصي بالصبر كذلك ضرورة . فالقيام على الإيمان والعمل الصالح ، وحراسة الحق والعدل

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r28.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r28.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r28.claim: Mutual exhortation to patience increases capacity through shared purpose, solidarity, love, resolve, and the communal conditions in which Islam is lived.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r28.anchor: والتواصي بالصبر يضاعف المقدرة ، بما يبعثه من إحساس بوحدة الهدف ، ووحدة المتجه

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r29.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r29.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r29.claim: Qutb sees worldly loss spreading because humanity turns away from God's good and lacks righteous authority; he says Muslims who claim Islam have strayed furthest from its guidance.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r29.anchor: يهولنا أن نرى الخسر يحيق بالبشرية في كل مكان على ظهر الأرض بلا استثناء

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r30.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r30.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r30.claim: The Arab lands that first received Islam abandoned its God-given banner for nationalist banners, although Islam had enabled Arabs to lead humanity righteously.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r30.anchor: البقاع التي انبعث منها هذا الخير أول مرة تترك الراية التي رفعها لها الله ، راية الإيمان

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r31.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r31.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r31.claim: Al-Nadwi presents the rise of Muslim leadership as an exceptionally righteous and beneficial chapter in human history.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r31.anchor: يقول الأستاذ أبو الحسن الندوي في كتابه القيم

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r32.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r32.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r32.claim: Al-Nadwi says Muslim leaders governed through revealed scripture and divine law rather than self-made legislation, with divine guidance for just rule.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r32.anchor: أولا : أنهم أصحاب كتاب منزل وشريعة إلهية ، فلا يقننون ولا يشترعون من عند أنفسهم

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r33.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r33.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r33.claim: Al-Nadwi says Muslim leaders received long moral and spiritual training under Muhammad before taking power, cultivating piety, honesty, selflessness, and fear of God.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r33.anchor: مكثوا زمنا طويلا تحت تربية محمد [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] وإشرافه الدقيق

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r34.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r34.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r34.claim: Al-Nadwi cites the rule that leadership should not be entrusted to a person who asks for office or eagerly seeks it.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r34.anchor: إنا والله لا نولي هذا العمل أحدا سأله ، أو أحدا حرص عليه

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r35.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r35.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r35.claim: Al-Nadwi says office was treated as a trust and divine test, with leaders accountable for justice and every matter entrusted to them.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r35.anchor: بل عدوه أمانة في عنقهم ، وامتحانا من الله

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r36.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r36.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r36.claim: Al-Nadwi rejects ethnic or national imperialism as the Muslim mission: its aim was to free all people from serving humans and direct them to God.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r36.anchor: ثالثا : أنهم لم يكونوا خدمة جنس ، ورسل شعب أو وطن

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r37.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r37.speaker: ربعي بن عامر
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r37.claim: At Yazdegerd's court, Rib'i ibn Amir described the Muslim mission as freeing people from human servitude, worldly confinement, and religious injustice.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r37.anchor: كما قال ربعي بن عامر رسول المسلمين في مجلس يزدجرد : الله ابتعثنا لنخرج الناس من عبادة العباد إلى عبادة الله وحده

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r38.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r38.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r38.claim: Al-Nadwi says all peoples are equal and honor rests in piety rather than ancestry, in keeping with the Qur'anic call to know one another.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r38.anchor: فالأمم عندهم سواء ، والناس عندهم سواء . الناس كلهم من آدم ، وآدم من تراب

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r39.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r39.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r39.claim: Qutb recounts Umar's order that an Egyptian whom the governor's son had struck receive redress, affirming that people are born free.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r39.anchor: وقد قال عمر بن الخطاب لعمرو بن العاص عامل مصر - وقد ضرب ابنه مصريا

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r40.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r40.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r40.claim: Al-Nadwi says Muslim rule shared religious learning, education, and government across peoples; many non-Arabs excelled and became leading scholars.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r40.anchor: في ظل هؤلاء وتحت حكمهم استطاعت الأمم والشعوب - حتى المضطهدة منها في القديم - أن تنال نصيبها من الدين والعلم

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r41.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r41.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r41.claim: Al-Nadwi argues that a sound civilization must nourish the whole person—body, spirit, heart, reason, emotions, and limbs—in balanced proportion.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r41.anchor: إن الإنسان جسم وروح ، وهو ذو قلب وعقل وعواطف وجوارح

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r42.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r42.speaker: أبو الحسن الندوي
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r42.claim: Al-Nadwi presents the Rightly Guided Caliphate as an ideal civilization joining spiritual, moral, religious, scientific, and material strengths, with strong social relations and relatively little crime.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r42.anchor: فلم نعرف دورا من أدوار التاريخ أكمل وأجمل وأزهر في جميع هذه النواحي من هذا الدور - دور الخلافة الراشدة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r43.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r43.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r43.claim: Earthly profit and loss are small beside the lasting stakes of Paradise and God's pleasure; the final loss is the collapse of human dignity.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r43.anchor: هناك الربح والخسر : ربح الجنة والرضوان ، أو خسر الجنة والرضوان

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r44.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r44.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r44.claim: The surah decisively sets one route out of loss: faith, righteous work, and a community that mutually guards truth with patience.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r44.anchor: طريق واحد لا يتعدد . طريق الإيمان والعمل الصالح وقيام الجماعة المسلمة

QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r45.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r45.speaker: الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r45.claim: Qutb reports that two Companions would not part after meeting until one recited Surat al-Asr to the other, renewing their commitment to its guidance.
QUTB-ZILAL:103:2/r45.anchor: كان الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] إذا التقيا لم يتفرقا حتى يقرأ أحدهما على الآخر سورة

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r1.claim: Al-ʿAṣr is Makkan and likely follows Sūrah 94; ʿaṣr can mean late afternoon, its last hour, afternoon, the afternoon prayer, or an epoch.

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r2.claim: Companions reportedly did not part after meeting until one recited the whole sūrah and greeted the other with peace.
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r2.anchor: whenever two Companions of the Prophet would meet they would not part company until one of them had recited al-ʿAṣr in its entirety

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.claim: Read after Sūrah 102, ʿaṣr can mean time generally: vying for increase wastes it, and time's blessing is what people will be questioned about.
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r3.anchor: When viewed in relation to the previous sūrah, ʿaṣr can be understood as a reference to time in general, meaning that vying for increase (102:1) prevents people from spending their time

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r4.claim: These three short verses can be seen as the whole Qur'an's message: humanity loses unless it turns to God.
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r4.anchor: From one perspective, these three short verses contain the entire message of the Quran, namely, that human beings are in loss unless they turn to God.

STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r5.speaker: al-Shāfiʿī
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī is reported to have said that if people pondered this sūrah, it would suffice them.
STUDYQURAN:103:intro/r5.anchor: the famous legal scholar al-Shāfiʿī is reported to have said,“Were the people to ponder this sūrah, it would suffice them”

STUDYQURAN:103:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r4.claim: This reading applies to individuals and humanity's history: each generation falls a degree below the previous one.
STUDYQURAN:103:1/r4.anchor: the fall of humanity continues as the historical cycle unfolds, and each generation is a degree below the generation before it.

STUDYQURAN:103:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r1.claim: Verses 2–3 answer the oath and parallel 95:5–6.
STUDYQURAN:103:2/r1.anchor: Vv. 2–3 are the response to the oath in v. 1 and are similar in meaning to 95:5–6

ASAD-NOTES:103:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:103:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:103:intro/r1.claim: The surah was revealed shortly after surah 94, Ash-Sharh.

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes the descent as Hell and exempts believers from that fate; Mujahid glosses the exception as those who believe.
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين إلا الذين آمنوا} [التين: 6] : إلا من آمن

TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.claim: Hasan reads the exception after Hell as parallel to the exception of believers from loss in Surat al-Asr.
TAB-FULL:v24p520/r5.anchor: قال الحسن، في قوله: {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين} [التين: 5] : «في النار» {إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} [التين: 6]

TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r7.claim: Mujahid explains the exception as those who believe.
TAB-FULL:v24p612#2/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {إن الإنسان لفي خسر} [العصر: 2] إلا من آمن "

TAB-FULL:v24p614/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p614/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p614/r1.claim: The exception means those who affirm God and His oneness, obey Him, fulfill obligations, and avoid what He forbids; they are excepted because ‘humanity’ is grammatically singular but means the collective human kind.
TAB-FULL:v24p614/r1.anchor: {إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات} [الشعراء: 227] يقول: إلا الذين صدقوا الله ووحدوه، وأقروا له بالوحدانية والطاعة، وعملوا الصالحات

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1.claim: The three-rhyme sura is an opening single-member oath by late afternoon, followed by a rebuke; verse 3 exempts believers and differentiates good from bad people.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:1-3:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die auf 3Kr reimende Sure besteht aus einem eingliedrigen Schwur „beim späten Nachmittag“ mit rügendem ʾinsān-Spruch als Schwuraussage

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.claim: The exception here requires faith and good works, whereas al-ʿAṣr adds mutual exhortation to truth and patience; that added practice prevents further loss of reward.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r16.anchor: فلم يقل مثل ما قال في سورة العصر: {والعصر * إِنَّ الإنسان لَفِى خُسْرٍ * إِلاَّ الذين آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصالحات

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r17.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r17.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r17.claim: Al-Tibyān says al-ʿAṣr narrows its exception because loss includes foregone reward from failing to exhort others, while this sura's exception is broader because exhortation is additional to personal faith and good works.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r17.anchor: فمن لم يكن كذلك فقد خسر هذا الربح فصار في خسر

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r18.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r18.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r18.claim: Al-Tibyān distinguishes duties one performs personally from the additional duty or merit of enjoining right and forbidding wrong, which can be individual, communal, or recommended.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r18.anchor: فإن الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر مرتبة زائدة. وقد تكون فرضاً على الأعيان. وقد تكون فرضاً على الكفاية

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r19.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r19.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r19.claim: Exhortation covers obligatory and recommended truth and patience; those who do it gain extra reward, while those who only meet personal duties lose that extra gain without being utterly ruined.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r17#2/r19.anchor: وإن كان أولئك لم يكونوا من الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم. فمطلق الخسارة شيء والخسار المطلق شيء

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r1.claim: The surah condenses Quranic teachings and gathers its aims in the briefest statement; although it could be Meccan or Medinan, it seems more likely Meccan.
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r1.anchor: تخلص السورة جميع المعارف القرآنية وتجمع شتات مقاصد القرآن في أوجز بيان

TABATABAI:103:1-3/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r11.claim: The exception is from humankind generally: those combining faith and righteous deeds are protected from loss.
TABATABAI:103:1-3/r11.anchor: استثناء من جنس الانسان الواقع في الخسر، والمستثنون هم الأفراد المتلبسون بالإيمان والأعمال الصالحة

TABATABAI:103:2-3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r1.claim: Earthly life is a test that determines the felicity or misery of the enduring afterlife.
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r1.anchor: ويبين أن شطرا من هذه الحياة وهي الحياة الدنيا حياة امتحانية تتعين بها صفة الشطر الأخير

TABATABAI:103:2-3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r2.claim: Belief and righteous action bring afterlife happiness, whereas disbelief and sin bring misery; life's capital is spent through belief and action, yielding profit by following truth or loss by following falsehood.
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r2.anchor: فالاعتقاد الحق والعمل الصالح ملاك السعادة الاخروية والكفر والفسوق ملاك الشقاء فيها

TABATABAI:103:2-3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r3.claim: Faith means belief in God, all His messengers, and the Last Day; denying any messenger or the Last Day is incompatible with belief in God.
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r3.anchor: والمراد بالإيمان الإيمان بالله ومن الإيمان بالله الإيمان بجميع رسله والإيمان باليوم الآخر

TABATABAI:103:2-3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:103:2-3/r4.claim: The apparent wording requires all righteous deeds, so sinful believers who omit some good are not wholly exempt: they lose in some respects, unlike obstinate disbelievers who lose in every respect and remain punished.
