CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r1.claim: The construction about mutual exhortation echoes 90:17, and the phrase about believers and good works is characteristic of late Meccan and Medinan texts; the verb amana is cross-referenced at 69:33.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Vgl. 90:17 (ṯumma kāna mina llaḏīna ʾāmanū wa-tawāṣau bi-ṣ-ṣabri wa-tawāṣau bi-l-marḥamah).

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r2.speaker: Medina II
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r2.claim: Medina II places a verse divider after haqq, yielding rhyme but separating two parallel, conceptually linked clauses, which Neuwirth objects to.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Medina II setzt einen Verstrenner nach ḥaqq (Spitaler, Verszählung, 35). Dabei ergäbe sich zwar ein Reim

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r3.claim: Neuwirth argues that the proposed divider separates two parallel clauses that belong together in thought.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r3.anchor: zwei gedanklich zusammengehörende und parallel gebaute Satzteile getrennt (Neuwirth, Studien, 35).

CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r4.claim: Because verse 3 is probably a later addition, its unusual length is unsurprising.
CORPUSCORANICUM:103:3:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Da V. 3 vermutlich ein späterer Zusatz ist (s. o.), ist die übermäßige Länge

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r1.speaker: أبو حاتم
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r1.claim: Abu Hatim reports that Abu Amr gives bāʾ in بالصبر a trace of kasra, but Ahmad ibn Musa says this is permitted only in a pause, not in connected reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو بالصبر يشم الباء شيئا من الجر ولا يشبع

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r2.speaker: سلام أبو المنذر
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r2.claim: Salam Abu al-Mundhir read والعصر with a kasra-like sound on ṣād; Abu Ali says the sound may mark a pause caused by breath or interruption.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r2.anchor: قال: سمعت سلاما أبا المنذر يقرأ: والعصر [1] فكسر الصاد، وهذا لا يجوز إلا في الوقف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r3.claim: Poetic examples show pause vowels carried into connection; the reported Kisai preference to color the nūn in منه and عنه is the same kind of pause feature.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r3.anchor: وأما ما روي عن الكسائي من استحبابه أن يشم النون في منه* وعنه*

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p438/r4.claim: العصر means either time in general or the day and night together; the paired expression العصران supports the latter meaning.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r1.claim: Believers who act righteously make a trade that cannot perish, exchanging fleeting, inferior goods for lasting, precious ones and righteous deeds for passing pleasures.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r1.anchor: فانهم في تجارة لن تبور حيث باعوا الفاني الخسيس واشتروا الباقي النفيس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r2.claim: The phrase ‘those who’ includes everyone meeting the description, not only ʿAlī and Salmān; Ibn ʿAbbās’s naming them makes them foremost examples, not an exclusive referent.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r2.anchor: والمراد بالموصول كل من اتصف بعنوان الصلة لا على كرم الله وجهه وسلمان الفارسي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r4.claim: Mutual exhortation to truth completes the believers’ care for others: they enjoin what is established and undeniable, whose good effects endure in both abodes, including faith in God and following His books and messengers in belief and action.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r4.anchor: وصى بعضهم بعضا بالامر الثابت الذي لا سبيل إلى انكاره ولا زوال في الدارين لمحاسن آثاره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r5.claim: Patience means resisting sins desired by human nature, sustaining difficult obedience, and bearing the afflictions God ordinarily sends.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r5.anchor: عن المعاصي التي تشتاق اليها النفس بحكم الجبلة البشرية وعلى الطاعات التي يشق عليها أداؤها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r6.claim: Patience is already included in truth, but is repeated with its own preposition and verb to emphasize special concern for it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r6.anchor: والصبر المذكور داخل في الحق وذكر بعده مع اعادة الجار والفعل المتعلق هو لابراز كمال العناية به

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, truth is the rank of worship—doing what pleases God—while patience is the rank of servitude: accepting what God does.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r7.anchor: ويجوز ان يكون الاول عبارة رتبة العبادة اتي هي فعل مايرضى الله تعالى والثاني عبارة رتبة العبودية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r8.claim: Patience is more than restraining oneself from desired action or omission: it is receiving what comes from God graciously and being inwardly and outwardly content with it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r8.anchor: ليس مجرد حبس النفس عما تتوق اليه من فعل أو ترك بل هو تلقي ما ورد منه عز وجل بالجميل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r9.speaker: سلام وهرون وابن موسى عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r9.claim: These transmitters read al-ʿaṣr with kasra on ṣād and al-ṣabr with kasra on bāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r9.anchor: وقرأ سلام وهرون وابن موسى عن أبي عمرو والعصر بكسر الصاد والصبر بكسر الباء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this vowel transfer is permissible only when stopping.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطية وهذا لايجوز الا في الوقف على نقل الحركة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r11.speaker: أبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r11.claim: A second transmission from Abū ʿAmr reads al-ṣabr with kasra on bāʾ and ishām; Ibn ʿAṭiyya likewise limits it to pause.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r11.anchor: وروى عن أبي عمرو بالصبر بكسر الباء اشماما وهذا كما قال لايكون أيضا الا في الوقف

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r12.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r12.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiʿ says ʿĪsā al-Baṣrī transferred the vowel of rāʾ to bāʾ in al-ṣabr, avoiding partial movement at pause and two consecutive vowelless letters; he calls it widespread Arabic, signaling inflection while preserving pause-sukūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r12.anchor: قرأ عيسى البصرة بالصبر بنقل حركة الراء إلى الباء لئلا يحتاج إلى أن يؤتى ببعض الحركة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r1.claim: Al-Baḥr cites the line ‘I am Jarīr, my kunya is Abū ʿAmr; I strike with the sword, and Saʿd at al-ʿaṣr’ as an example of this usage.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r2.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r2.claim: ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and others report that Companion ʿAlī recited an expanded form, adding ‘نوائب الدهر’ after al-ʿaṣr and extending the phrase with ‘إلى آخر الدهر’.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r2.anchor: عن علي كرم الله وجهه أنه كان يقرأوالعصر نوائب الدهر ان الانان لفي خسر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r3.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r3.claim: ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī Dāwūd in al-Maṣāḥif report that Maymūn b. Mihrān recited the extended phrase ‘إلى آخر الدهر’; he identified it as Ibn Masʿūd’s reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r3.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران أنه قرأ والعصر ان الانسان لفي خسر وانه لفيه إلى آخر الدهر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r4.speaker: بعض المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r4.claim: Some Muʿtazilites infer that a major sinner remains eternally in Hell because the sura exempts from loss only believers who act righteously and exhort to truth and patience.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r4.anchor: استدل بعض المعتزلة بما في هذه السورة على ان مرتكب الكبيرة مخلد في النار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r5.claim: Alusi answers that the passage establishes only that those not excepted are in loss, not eternal punishment: loss may mean eternal residence for an unbeliever, entry into Hell for an unforgiven sinner, or lost high ranks if forgiven; he calls this a sound answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r5.anchor: وأجيب عنه بانه لا دلالة في ذلك على أكثر من كون غير المستثنى في خسر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r6.speaker: الماتريدى
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r6.claim: Al-Māturīdī offers further responses in al-Taʾwīlāt, but Alusi calls them strained elaborations.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r6.anchor: وللشيخ الماتريدى رحمه الله تعالى في التفصى عن ذلك تكلفات مذكورة في التأويلات

ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r7.claim: The sura plainly urges commanding right, forbidding wrong, and wishing for one’s brother what one wishes for oneself.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p229/r7.anchor: وفي السورة من الندب إلى الامر بالمعروف والنهي عن النكر وان يحب المرء لاخيه مايحب لنفسه

BINTSHATI:v2p82/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r1.claim: Across Qur'anic uses, al-insān denotes a morally accountable human tested by good and evil, temptation, vanity, and tyranny, bearing obligations beyond being simply one of humankind.
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r1.anchor: في سياق الأهلية لاحتمال تبعات التكليف، والابتلاء بالخير والشر

BINTSHATI:v2p82/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r2.claim: The Qur'an gives al-insān knowledge, articulate expression, and disputation and makes it the bearer of admonition and trust.
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r2.anchor: الإنسان في القرآن الكريم، لا الإنس، هو الذي أختص بالعلم

BINTSHATI:v2p82/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r3.speaker: الراغب الأصفهاني
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib connects the word insān with sociability and familiarity with a group; the author accepts this as fitting Arabic usage.
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r3.anchor: وللراغب الأصفهاني ملحظ دقيق في اشتقاق لفظ الإنسان

BINTSHATI:v2p82/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r4.claim: In al-ʿAṣr the word denotes human responsibility for the burdens of obligation, individually and socially.
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r4.anchor: في سورة العصر، في سياق ما يحتمل من تبعات التكليف

BINTSHATI:v2p82/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r5.claim: Khusr opposes profit, first denoting commercial loss, then deficiency, injustice, weakness, betrayal, or fraud, and religiously deviation from truth.
BINTSHATI:v2p82/r5.anchor: والخسر لغة نقيض الربح، استعمل مادياً في التجارة الخاسرة

BINTSHATI:v2p83/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p83/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p83/r1.claim: Khusr applies materially to trade and measurement and morally to Joseph's brothers and Cain, but most Qur'anic uses warn of religious error and punishment.
BINTSHATI:v2p83/r1.anchor: والغالب لأن يأتي الخسر بالمعنى الديني، في سياق النذير بسوء العقبى

BINTSHATI:v2p83/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p83/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p83/r2.claim: Loss may encompass self, wealth, family, and deeds and is especially clear at resurrection as loss of both worlds.
BINTSHATI:v2p83/r2.anchor: ويؤذن السياق فيها بأن الخسر يتعلق بالنفس والمال والأهل والعمل

BINTSHATI:v2p83/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p83/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p83/r3.claim: Examples include the failed at God's judgment, those who lose themselves and their families at resurrection, and those whose work is nullified by disbelief.
BINTSHATI:v2p83/r3.anchor: الذين خسروا أنفسهم وأهليهم يوم القيامة

BINTSHATI:v2p84/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r1.claim: The Qur'an calls those who obstruct God's path and disbelieve in the afterlife the greatest losers and describes Satan's party as losers.
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r1.anchor: أربع مرات للذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجاً

BINTSHATI:v2p84/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r2.claim: Khusrān mubīn describes taking Satan as patron and conditional worship that turns away after hardship; the author adds al-Zumar as a parallel.
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r2.anchor: فجاء بصيغة خسران ثلاث مرات، موصوفاً فيها بالمبين

BINTSHATI:v2p84/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r3.claim: Khasār is used of Noah's people, wrongdoers, and disbelievers; takhsīr appears in Hūd, while khusr occurs in al-ʿAṣr and al-Ṭalāq for ruin from error and rebellion.
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r3.anchor: وبصيغة الخسار، ثلاث مرات كذلك، في قوم نوح

BINTSHATI:v2p84/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r4.claim: The survey distinguishes religious loss from material loss while tracing the Qur'anic forms of the root.
BINTSHATI:v2p84/r4.anchor: وهذا الاستقراء يتيح لنا أن نقول إن الخسر يأتي في القرآن

BINTSHATI:v2p85/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p85/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p85/r1.claim: She rejects al-Rāghib's claim that all Qur'anic khusr concerns faith and never property or trade, since some contexts explicitly concern measurement.

BINTSHATI:v2p85/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p85/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p85/r2.claim: She rejects al-Zamakhsharī's trade metaphor in which everyone loses a worldly bargain except the righteous who buy the afterlife.

BINTSHATI:v2p85/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p85/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p85/r3.claim: She also declines al-Rāzī's claim that everyone loses by wasting life's capital, even through permissible acts or imperfect worship.

BINTSHATI:v2p85/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p85/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p85/r4.claim: The explicit exception means believers who act righteously and counsel truth and patience are never in loss.
BINTSHATI:v2p85/r4.anchor: وصريح النص في الآية بعد الخسر

BINTSHATI:v2p86/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r3.claim: Īmān opposes disbelief and carries the original sense of security and trust; ṣāliḥāt are religious good works opposed to sins.
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r3.anchor: الإيمان نقيض الكفر، وفي دلالته اللغوية الأصلية حس الأمن والأمانة

BINTSHATI:v2p86/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r4.claim: The verse makes faith and good works individual duties, and mutual counsel in truth and patience a communal responsibility.
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r4.anchor: على الإنسان مسئوليته فرداً بالإيمان وعمل الصالحات

BINTSHATI:v2p86/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r5.claim: The Qur'an often pairs faith and good works, promising believers safety, good life, reward, forgiveness, provision, succession, affection, and Paradise.
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r5.anchor: ويقترن العمل الصالح بالإيمان في القرآن الكريم نحو خمس وسبعين مرة

BINTSHATI:v2p86/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r6.claim: Good works are attributed to messengers and righteous people and appear in the prayers of Joseph, Abraham, and Solomon.
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r6.anchor: ويأتي العمل الصالح مسنداً إلى رسل الله

BINTSHATI:v2p86/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r7.claim: The author links good works with rejecting shirk in al-Kahf and contrasts them with disbelief in al-Rūm.
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r7.anchor: وعطف النهي عن الشرك على العمل الصالح

BINTSHATI:v2p87/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p87/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p87/r1.claim: Muʿtazilites and Ashʿarites disputed whether works are called righteous because they intrinsically embody goodness or because God commanded them.
BINTSHATI:v2p87/r1.anchor: كالذي ثار بين المعتزلة والأشعرية من خلاف حول تسمية الأعمال بالصالحات

BINTSHATI:v2p87/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p87/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p87/r2.claim: Some argue that coordinating good works with faith proves works are outside faith, since otherwise it repeats the same idea; they reject examples that restate an honorable subset after a general term.
BINTSHATI:v2p87/r2.anchor: الوقوف عند عطف عمل الصالحاتعلى الإيمان

BINTSHATI:v2p87/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p87/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p87/r3.claim: Their opponents note that the same sūrah coordinates mutual counsel in truth and patience after good works and allow repetition for emphasis, while conceding that repetition is not the default.
BINTSHATI:v2p87/r3.anchor: لا نمنع التكرير لأجل التأكيد. ولكن الأصل عدمه

BINTSHATI:v2p87/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p87/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p87/r4.claim: Her survey shows that faith is often followed by good works, signaling that faith should be joined to action rather than making the coordination empty repetition.

BINTSHATI:v2p88/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p88/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p88/r1.claim: Al-ḥaqq is the opposite of falsehood; Arabic uses it for a straight thrust, tightly woven cloth, and a mature camel, then for justice, truth, and fate.

BINTSHATI:v2p88/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p88/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p88/r2.claim: The root's sense of firmness develops into truth and religious use as a divine name, revelation, and religion.
BINTSHATI:v2p88/r2.anchor: ومن ثم شاع استعماله في نقيض الباطل

BINTSHATI:v2p88/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p88/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p88/r3.claim: Even if righteous works are included in faith, their separate mention is specification after generality, highlighting the value and place of good works.
BINTSHATI:v2p88/r3.anchor: فيه تنبيه إلى قيمة عمل الصالحات

BINTSHATI:v2p89/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r1.claim: Tawāṣī means people counsel one another; its root conveys strong connection, as in a palm frond used for binding and a bequest that conveys an instruction to its recipient.
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r1.anchor: والتواصي: أن يوصى بعضهم بعضاً. والأصل اللغوي للمادة يعطي معنى قوة

BINTSHATI:v2p89/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r2.claim: The Qur'an uses waṣṣā and awṣā for divine instruction and often a testament; tawāṣaw occurs five times, including the question whether earlier peoples conspired to reject messengers.
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r2.anchor: أما التواضي فجاء في القرآن خمس مرات

BINTSHATI:v2p89/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r3.claim: Rights involving wealth and family law carry religious sanctity and Resurrection is named al-Ḥāqqah.
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r3.anchor: بما لهذه الحقوق من حرمة دينية تجعلها من حدود الله

BINTSHATI:v2p89/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r4.claim: The Qur'anic term includes divinely protected rights in wealth, inheritance, marriage, and divorce.
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r4.anchor: ما فرض الله على ذوي المال من حق معلوم

BINTSHATI:v2p89/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p89/r5.claim: The religious weight of ḥaqq gives it awe and solemnity in mutual counsel.

BINTSHATI:v2p90/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Balad also links faith and mutual counsel in patience and compassion after freeing a slave or feeding the needy; both Meccan sūrahs state foundational teachings.
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r1.anchor: ثم كان من الذين آمنوا وتواصوا بالصبر وتواصوا بالمرحمة

BINTSHATI:v2p90/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r2.claim: Ṣabr opposes panic; its concrete senses include bitter sap, sour milk, coarse stones, severe war or calamity, cold, restraint, and execution while bound.
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r2.anchor: والصبر في العربية نقيض الجزع. ومن استعماله في الحسيات

BINTSHATI:v2p90/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r3.speaker: الإمام الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains patience as perseverance in obedience; al-Zamakhsharī includes avoiding sins, obeying, and enduring God's tests, with Abū Ḥayyān close.
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r3.anchor: وقد فسره الإمام الطبري بالصبر على العمل بطاعة الله

BINTSHATI:v2p90/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r4.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī says patience includes fulfilling duties and avoiding prohibitions, since both doing what is disliked and restraining desire are hard; truth is burdensome and accompanied by trials.
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r4.anchor: إن التواصي بالصبر يدخل فيه حمل النفس على مشقة التكليف

BINTSHATI:v2p90/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p90/r5.claim: She accepts these as close interpretations, scarcely different from Muḥammad ʿAbduh's commentary.

BINTSHATI:v2p91/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r1.claim: God commands the Prophet to endure the burdens of conveying his message and facing rejection and verbal or physical harm in about twenty passages.
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r1.anchor: من أعباء تبليغ رسالته، ما يلقى من تكذيب وأذى

BINTSHATI:v2p91/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r2.claim: Believers are told to seek God's aid through patience and prayer and persevere in battle.
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r2.anchor: وأمر الله المؤمنين بأن يستعينوا بالله، وبالصبر والصلاة

BINTSHATI:v2p91/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r3.claim: Patience is attributed to prophets, resolute messengers, earlier messengers, guiding leaders, and believers rewarded with a good final home.
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r3.anchor: وجاء الصبر مسنداً إلى أولي العزم من الرسل

BINTSHATI:v2p91/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r4.claim: Patience verses address prophets and believers, apart from warnings to the lost that patience or panic in Hell will not help.
BINTSHATI:v2p91/r4.anchor: وآيات الصبر في القرآن الكريم لا تتجه إلى غير هذه الصفوة

BINTSHATI:v2p92/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r1.claim: The Qur'an also depicts idolaters persisting in their idols, error, and disbelief.
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r1.anchor: وقريب منها صبر المشركين على آلهتهم

BINTSHATI:v2p92/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r2.claim: Believers' patience bears on trials, calamities, hardship, warfare, migration after persecution, and steadfastness; God loves and accompanies the patient.
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r2.anchor: ومما يتعلق به صبر المؤمنين: الابتلاء

BINTSHATI:v2p92/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r3.claim: Leaving patience's object unstated in al-ʿAṣr and al-Balad broadens it to Qur'anic demands including faith, testing, ease, hardship, and battle.
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r3.anchor: والسكوت عن ذكر متعلق الصبر الذي يتواصى به الذين آمنوا

BINTSHATI:v2p92/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r4.claim: Mutual counsel in truth and patience is a religious duty to the community, covering obligations, testing, prosperity, hardship, and combat.
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r4.anchor: مما يصبر عليه المؤمنين من تكاليف الإيمان، والإبتلاء

BINTSHATI:v2p92/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r5.claim: The Qur'an rejects passive individualism: faith and good deeds alone do not discharge the communal duty; righteous individuals benefit society by avoiding harm to others.
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r5.anchor: وموقف القرآن من هذه التبعية، يقطع برفض السلبية

BINTSHATI:v2p92/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r6.claim: The author questions whether merely professing the testimony, worshipping, and avoiding wrongdoing can suffice; the passage ends before completing the thought.
BINTSHATI:v2p92/r6.anchor: أن الإيمان يكفي فيه النطق بالشهادتين وأداء العبادات

TAB:103:3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:3/r1.speaker: author
TAB:103:3/r1.claim: The exception is those who believe God, affirm His oneness, and acknowledge their duty to obey Him.

TAB:103:3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:3/r2.speaker: author
TAB:103:3/r2.claim: Good deeds mean performing the duties God made obligatory and avoiding the sins He prohibited.
TAB:103:3/r2.anchor: وعملوا الصالحات ،   وأدوا ما لزمهم من فرائضه ،   واجتنبوا ما نهاهم عنه من معاصيه

TAB:103:3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:3/r3.speaker: author
TAB:103:3/r3.claim: The exception qualifies al-insān because “the human” here denotes humanity collectively, not one individual.
TAB:103:3/r3.anchor: واستثنى الذين آمنوا عن الإنسان ؛ لأن الإنسان بمعنى الجمع ،   لا بمعنى الواحد

TAB:103:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:3/r4.speaker: author
TAB:103:3/r4.claim: They counsel one another to follow what God revealed in His Book, carrying out its commands and avoiding its prohibitions.
TAB:103:3/r4.anchor: وأوصى بعضهم بعضا بلزوم العمل بما أنزل الله في كتابه ،   من أمره ،   واجتناب ما نهى عنه فيه

TAB:103:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:3/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB:103:3/r5.claim: Qatada identifies the truth they counsel one another to follow as God's Book.
TAB:103:3/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {  وتواصوا بالحق } والحق :  كتاب الله

TAB:103:3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:3/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB:103:3/r6.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the truth they counsel one another to follow as God's Book.
TAB:103:3/r6.anchor: سمعت الحسن يقول في {  وتواصوا بالحق } قال :  الحق :  كتاب الله

TAB:103:3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:3/r7.speaker: author
TAB:103:3/r7.claim: They counsel one another to be patient in carrying out obedience to God.
TAB:103:3/r7.anchor: وأوصى بعضهم بعضا بالصبر على العمل بطاعة الله

TAB:103:3/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:3/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB:103:3/r8.claim: Qatada glosses patience as obedience to God.
TAB:103:3/r8.anchor: عن قتادة {  وتواصوا بالصبر } قال :  الصبر :  طاعة الله

TAB:103:3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:3/r9.speaker: الحسن
TAB:103:3/r9.claim: Al-Hasan glosses patience as obedience to God.
TAB:103:3/r9.anchor: سمعت الحسن يقول في قوله {  وتواصوا بالصبر } قال :  الصبر :  طاعة الله

DAMGHANI:v1p137/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p137/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p137/r13.claim: The entry lists twelve senses of al-ḥaqq: God, Qur’an, Islam, justice, monotheism, truth, obligation, reality, wealth, priority, share, and need.
DAMGHANI:v1p137/r13.anchor: ح ف ق على اثني عشر وجها الله القرآن الإسلام العدل التوحيد الصدق حق وجب الحق بعينه الذي ليس بباطل المال أولى الحظ الحاجة

DAMGHANI:v1p137/r14.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p137/r14.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p137/r14.claim: The first sense here is God: in 23:71, the heavens and earth would be corrupted if God followed their desires; in 103:3, believers urge one another toward God alone.
DAMGHANI:v1p137/r14.anchor: فوجه منها : الحق يعني الله قوله تعالى في سورة المؤمنين " ولو اتبع الحق أهواءهم لفسدت السموات والأرض " يعني لو اتبع الله سبحانه أهواء المشركين

ABUHAYYAN:103:1/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:1/r9.speaker: سلام
ABUHAYYAN:103:1/r9.claim: Salām reads al-ʿaṣr with a kasra on ṣād and al-ṣabr with a kasra on bāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN:103:1/r9.anchor: وقرأ سلام : والعصر بكسر الصاد ،   والصبر بكسر الباء

ABUHAYYAN:103:1/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:1/r11.speaker: هارون وابن موسى عن أبي عمرو
ABUHAYYAN:103:1/r11.claim: Al-Kāmil reports Harūn and Ibn Mūsā from Abū ʿAmr reading al-ʿaṣr, al-ṣabr, al-fajr, and al-watr with a vowel before the quiescent consonant; others read them with sukūn.
ABUHAYYAN:103:1/r11.anchor: وفي الكامل للهزلي : والعصر ،   والصبر ،   والفجر ،   والوتر ،   بكسر ما قبل الساكن في هذه كلها هارون وابن موسى عن أبي عمرو

ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r1.claim: A report from Abū ʿAmr gives al-ṣabr with a kasra on bāʾ by ishmām, a form that occurs only in pausing.
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r1.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو : بالصبر بكسر الباء إشماما ،   وهذا أيضا لا يكون إلا في الوقف

ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r2.speaker: ابن خالويه
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r2.claim: Ibn Khālawayh describes Abū ʿAmr’s form as transferring the vowel.
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r2.anchor: وقال ابن خالويه : { وتواصوا بالصبر } ،   بنقل الحركة عن أبي عمرو

ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r3.speaker: عيسى صاحب اللوامح
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r3.claim: ʿĪsā of al-Lawāmiḥ explains the reading as transferring a vowel to avoid a partial vowel at pause or two adjacent sukūns; he calls the usage widespread and a marker of inflection.
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r3.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح عيسى : البصرة بالصبر ،   بنقل حركة الهاء إلى الياء لئلا يحتاج أن يأتي ببعض الحركة في الوقف

ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r4.claim: A rajaz line pronouncing Abū ʿUmar for Abū ʿAmr illustrates the transferred-vowel phenomenon.
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r4.anchor: أنا جرير كنيتي أبو عمر *** أضرب بالسيف وسعد في العصر يريد : أبو عمر

ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r5.claim: The believers counsel one another in the established truth, which they themselves practice and enjoin.
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r5.anchor: { وتواصوا بالحق } : أي بالأمر الثابت من الذين عملوا به وتواصوا به ،

ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r6.claim: They counsel one another to be patient in obedience to God and away from sins.
ABUHAYYAN:103:3/r6.anchor: { وتواصوا بالصبر } في طاعة الله تعالى ،   وعن المعاصي

ALUSI:103:3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:3/r1.claim: Believers who do good deeds make a trade that will not fail, exchanging fleeting inferior goods for lasting precious ones and enduring good deeds.
ALUSI:103:3/r1.anchor: فإنهم في تجارة لن تبور حيث باعوا الفاني الخسيس واشتروا الباقي النفيس

ALUSI:103:3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:3/r2.claim: The relative phrase includes everyone with these traits, not only ʿAlī and Salmān, whom Ibn ʿAbbās names; they are foremost among those included.
ALUSI:103:3/r2.anchor: والمراد بالموصول كل من اتصف بعنوان الصلة لا علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وسلمان الفارسي

ALUSI:103:3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:3/r3.claim: Mutual counsel in truth completes others: truth is what cannot be denied or lose its lasting good, encompassing faith in God and following revealed books and messengers in belief and action.
ALUSI:103:3/r3.anchor: أي وصى بعضاً بالأمر الثابت الذي لا سبيل إلى إنكاره ولا زوال في الدارين لمحاسن آثاره

ALUSI:103:3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:3/r4.claim: Patience means resisting sins desired by human nature, sustaining difficult acts of obedience, and enduring the afflictions God sends.
ALUSI:103:3/r4.anchor: عن المعاصي التي تشتاق إليها النفس بحكم الجبلة البشرية وعلى الطاعات التي يشق عليها أداؤها وعلى ما يبتلى الله تعالى به عباده من المصائب

ALUSI:103:3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:3/r5.claim: Patience is already part of truth, but is repeated with its own verb and preposition to emphasize special care for it.
ALUSI:103:3/r5.anchor: والصبر المذكور داخل في الحق وذكر بعده مع إعادة الجار والفعل المتعلق هو به لإبراز كمال العناية به

ALUSI:103:3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:3/r6.claim: A possible reading makes truth the rank of worship, doing what pleases God, and patience the rank of servitude, accepting God's acts with inward and outward contentment.
ALUSI:103:3/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الأول عبارة رتبة العبادة التي هي فعل ما يرضى الله تعالى والثاني عبارة رتبة العبودية

ALUSI:103:3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:3/r7.claim: Patience is more than restraining desire: it is receiving God's decree gracefully and being content with it inwardly and outwardly.
ALUSI:103:3/r7.anchor: فإن المراد بالصبر ليس مجرد حبس النفس عما تتوق إليه من فعل أو ترك بل هو تلقي ما ورد منه عز وجل بالجميل

ALUSI:103:3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r8.speaker: سلام وهرون وابن موسى عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI:103:3/r8.claim: Salām, Hārūn, and Ibn Mūsā from Abū ʿAmr read al-ʿaṣr with a kasra on ṣād and al-ṣabr with a kasra on bāʾ; Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows this only at pause by vowel transfer.
ALUSI:103:3/r8.anchor: وقرأ سلام وهرون وابن موسى عن أبي عمرو والعصر بكسر الصاد والصبر بكسر الباء

ALUSI:103:3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI:103:3/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the kasra reading can only occur at pause through transferring the vowel, and likewise rejects the reported ishām kasra except at pause.
ALUSI:103:3/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطية وهذا لا يجوز ألا في الوقف على نقل الحركة

ALUSI:103:3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
ALUSI:103:3/r10.claim: A report from Abū ʿAmr gives al-ṣabr a kasra with ishām; Ibn ʿAṭiyya likewise says this is only at pause.
ALUSI:103:3/r10.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو بالصبر بكسر الباء اشماما

ALUSI:103:3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r11.speaker: عيسى البصرة
ALUSI:103:3/r11.claim: ʿĪsā al-Baṣrī transfers the rāʾ vowel to bāʾ to avoid partial movement at pause or two consecutive quiescent letters; the lexeme is a common language form.
ALUSI:103:3/r11.anchor: قرأ عيسى البصرة بالصبر بنقل حركة الراء إلى الباء لئلا يحتاج

ALUSI:103:3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:3/r12.claim: A line ascribed to Jarīr illustrates the transferred vowel in the expression bi-l-ʿaṣr.
ALUSI:103:3/r12.anchor: ومن هذا كما في البحر قوله

ALUSI:103:3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r13.speaker: علي
ALUSI:103:3/r13.claim: A report attributes to ʿAlī a reading adding nawāʾib al-dahr and extending the loss statement to the end of time.
ALUSI:103:3/r13.anchor: عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه كان يقرى والعصر ونوائب الدهر إن الإنسان لفي خسر

ALUSI:103:3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r14.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
ALUSI:103:3/r14.claim: Maymūn ibn Mihrān reports a reading ascribed to Ibn Masʿūd that says the person remains in loss until the end of time, except those who believe.
ALUSI:103:3/r14.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران أنه قرأ والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر وإنه لفيه إلى آخر الدهر

ALUSI:103:3/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r15.speaker: بعض المعتزلة
ALUSI:103:3/r15.claim: Some Muʿtazilites infer that a grave sinner remains eternally in Hell because only believers who do good are excepted from loss.
ALUSI:103:3/r15.anchor: واستدل بعض المعتزلة بما في هذه السورة على أن مرتكب الكبيرة مخلد في النار

ALUSI:103:3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:3/r16.claim: Al-Ālūsī replies that the verse puts everyone outside the exception in loss, not necessarily eternal Hell: loss may mean Hell for an unpardoned sinner or missed highest ranks if forgiven.
ALUSI:103:3/r16.anchor: وأما على كونه مخلداً في النار فلا كيف والخسر عام

ALUSI:103:3/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r17.speaker: الماتريدي
ALUSI:103:3/r17.claim: Al-Māturīdī offers further ways to answer the objection in al-Taʾwīlāt, but al-Ālūsī calls them strained.
ALUSI:103:3/r17.anchor: وللشيخ الماتريدي رحمه الله تعالى في التفصي عن ذلك تكلفات مذكورة في التأويلات

ALUSI:103:3/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:3/r18.claim: The sūra clearly urges enjoining right, forbidding wrong, and wishing for one's brother what one wishes for oneself.
ALUSI:103:3/r18.anchor: وفي السورة من الندب إلى الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر وان يحب المرء لأخيه ما يحب لنفسه

BAGHAWI:103:3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:103:3/r1.claim: Those who believe and do righteous works are not among the losers.
BAGHAWI:103:3/r1.anchor: إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات } فإنهم ليسوا في خسر

BAGHAWI:103:3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:3/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:103:3/r2.claim: Tawāṣaw means that they enjoin or counsel one another.

BAGHAWI:103:3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:3/r3.speaker: الحسن، قتادة
BAGHAWI:103:3/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada explain truth as the Qur’an.

BAGHAWI:103:3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:3/r4.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI:103:3/r4.claim: Muqatil explains truth as faith and the oneness of God.

BAGHAWI:103:3/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:3/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:103:3/r5.claim: Patience means persevering in the obligations and establishing God’s command.
BAGHAWI:103:3/r5.anchor: وتواصوا بالصبر } على أداء الفرائض وإقامة أمر الله

BAGHAWI:103:3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:3/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
BAGHAWI:103:3/r6.claim: Ibrahim, as related by Ibn ʿAwn, says aging and frailty diminish a person, except believers retain the recorded rewards and good works of their youth and health.
BAGHAWI:103:3/r6.anchor: وروى ابن عون عن إبراهيم قال : أراد أن الإنسان إذا عمر في الدنيا وهرم ، لفي نقص وتراجع إلا المؤمنين

BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.claim: Baghawi connects Ibrahim’s account of believers retaining their good works in old age with the passage about creation in the best form and the exception of believers from being brought low.
BAGHAWI:103:3/r7.anchor: وهي مثل قوله : { لقد خلقنا الإنسان في أحسن تقويم * ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين * إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات }

BAYDAWI:103:3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:103:3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:103:3/r1.claim: Believers who do righteous deeds trade the world for the afterlife and win eternal life and everlasting happiness.
BAYDAWI:103:3/r1.anchor: فإنهم اشتروا الآخرة بالدنيا ، ففازوا بالحياة الأبدية ، والسعادة السرمدية

BAYDAWI:103:3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:103:3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:103:3/r2.claim: Truth is what cannot rightly be denied, in belief or action.
BAYDAWI:103:3/r2.anchor: الثابت الذي لا يصح إنكاره من اعتقاد أو عمل

BAYDAWI:103:3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:103:3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:103:3/r3.claim: Patience means abstaining from sins, steadfastness on truth, or enduring what God tests His servants with.
BAYDAWI:103:3/r3.anchor: عن المعاصي ، أو على الحق ، أو ما يبلو الله به عباده

BAYDAWI:103:3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:103:3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:103:3/r4.claim: Mentioning truth and patience coordinates specific qualities with the general category for emphasis, unless deeds are restricted to acts that perfect the individual alone.
BAYDAWI:103:3/r4.anchor: وهذا من عطف الخاص على العام للمبالغة ، إلا أن يخص العمل بما يكون مقصورا على كماله

BAYDAWI:103:3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:103:3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:103:3/r5.claim: He mentions the cause of profit without spelling out loss, to state the aim, imply other paths bring loss or a diminished share, and graciously leave loss implicit.
BAYDAWI:103:3/r5.anchor: بأن ما عد إما عد يؤدي إلى خسر ونقص حظ ، أو تكرما ، فإن الإبهام في جانب الخسر كرم

BAYDAWI:103:3/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:103:3/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI:103:3/r6.claim: A report from the Prophet says reciting Sūrat al-ʿAṣr earns forgiveness and places the reciter among those who counsel one another in truth and patience; no grading is stated.
BAYDAWI:103:3/r6.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :  " من قرأ سورة ( والعصر ) غفر الله له ، وكان ممن تواصوا بالحق وتواصوا بالصبر

BIQAI:103:3/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r1.claim: The exception saves the few whom God protects from humanity's default defects; the general judgment applies because people have no innate claim to exemption.
BIQAI:103:3/r1.anchor: ولما كان الحكم على الجنس حكماً على الكل ؛ لأنهم ليس لهم من ذواتهم إلا ذلك ، وكان فيهم من خلصه الله سبحانه وتعالى مما طبع عليه الإنسان

BIQAI:103:3/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r2.speaker: حديث صحيح
BIQAI:103:3/r2.claim: Biqāʿī invokes a sound hadith saying the saved are one among a thousand; no chain authority is named here.
BIQAI:103:3/r2.anchor: فالمخلص واحد من ألف كما في الحديث الصحيح

BIQAI:103:3/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r3.claim: Faith is assent to what is necessarily known to have come with the Prophet: God's oneness, angels, scriptures, messengers, and the Last Day.
BIQAI:103:3/r3.anchor: وهو التصديق بما علم بالضرورة مجيء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم به من توحيده سبحانه وتعالى والتصديق بملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر

BIQAI:103:3/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r4.claim: The past-tense form encourages entry into the religion even at its lowest degree and promises escape from loss to whoever meets its conditions.
BIQAI:103:3/r4.anchor: ولعل حكمة التعبير بالماضي الحث على الدخول في الدين ولو على أدنى الدرجات ، والبشارة لمن فعل ذلك بشرطه بالنجاة من الخسر

BIQAI:103:3/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r5.claim: Righteous works confirm professed faith: obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions in worship, such as prayer, and everyday dealings, such as sales.
BIQAI:103:3/r5.anchor: وهو اتباع الأوامر واجتناب النواهي في العبادات كالصلاة والعادات كالبيع

BIQAI:103:3/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r6.claim: By these works believers trade the world for the afterlife; worldly competition no longer distracts them, and they attain eternal life and happiness.
BIQAI:103:3/r6.anchor: فاشتروا الآخرة بالدنيا ، فلم يلههم التكاثر ، ففازوا بالحياة الأبدية والسعادة السرمدية

BIQAI:103:3/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r7.claim: Personal good works alone do not remove all loss: prophets were sent to perfect others, and religion is completed through collective enjoining of right and forbidding wrong.
BIQAI:103:3/r7.anchor: ولما كان الإنسان بعد كماله في نفسه بالأعمال لا ينتفي عنه مطلق الخسر إلا بتكميل غيره ، وحينئذ يكون وارثاً ؛ لأن الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام بعثوا للتكميل

BIQAI:103:3/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r8.claim: Religion stands and reaches completion through enjoining right and forbidding wrong, which arise from the heart's light and require community.
BIQAI:103:3/r8.anchor: وكان الدين لا يقوم ، وإذا قام لا يتم إلا بالأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر الناشىء عن نور القلب ، ولا يتأتى ذلك إلا بالاجتماع

BIQAI:103:3/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r9.claim: Mutual counsel can be conveyed by word or conduct; al-ḥaqq is whatever sacred law judges sound, whether speech, action, belief, doing, or leaving something.
BIQAI:103:3/r9.anchor: وهو كل ما حكم الشرع بصحته فلا يصح بوجه نفيه من قول أو عمل أو اعتقاد

BIQAI:103:3/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r10.claim: Those who uphold right face hostility from aggressors, the majority in every age, so believers also need to counsel one another to patience.
BIQAI:103:3/r10.anchor: ولما كان الإنسان ميالاً إلى النقصان ، فكان فاعل ذلك الإحسان معرضاً للشنآن من أهل العدوان ، وهم الأغلب في كل زمان

BIQAI:103:3/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r11.claim: Patience purifies practical life: obeying God, establishing truth, undoing falsehood, bearing resulting harm, and avoiding evil until death leads to the Abode of Peace.
BIQAI:103:3/r11.anchor: الناشىء عن زكاة النفس على العمل بطاعة الله من إحقاق الحق وإبطال الباطل والنفي له والمحق

BIQAI:103:3/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r12.claim: Worship has an outward end, Paradise, and an inward end, the light that brings the worshipper near to God; patience preserves knowledge while completing practice.
BIQAI:103:3/r12.anchor: وهي هنا أمران : خارج عن العامل وهو الجنة ، وداخل قائم به وهو النور المقرب من الحق سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI:103:3/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r13.claim: Calling it mutual counsel signals gentleness and the strongest effort to use kindness when enjoining right and forbidding wrong.
BIQAI:103:3/r13.anchor: واختير التعبير بالوصية إشارة إلى الرفق في الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر ، واستعمال اللين بغاية الجهد

BIQAI:103:3/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r14.claim: Patience is the human essence and finest extract, reached by pressing the self, compelling obedience, and training it to follow Sunna and the community.
BIQAI:103:3/r14.anchor: والصبر هو خلاصة الإنسان وسره وصفاوته وزبدته وعصارته الذي لا يوصل إليه إلا بضغط الإنسان لنفسه

BIQAI:103:3/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r15.claim: The fourteen words of the verse point to year fourteen of the prophetic mission, when jihad was permitted, identified with the Hijra year.
BIQAI:103:3/r15.anchor: وهي أربع عشرة كلمة تشير إلى أن في السنة الرابعة عشرة من النبوة يكون الإذن في الجهاد الذي هو رأس الأمر بالمعروف بالفعل

BIQAI:103:3/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r16.claim: Adding the four words of the basmala makes eighteen, which Biqāʿī associates numerically with year five AH and the Badr al-Mawʿid and Confederates campaigns.
BIQAI:103:3/r16.anchor: فإذا ضممت إليها أربع كلمات البسملة كانت موازية في العدد لسنة خمس من الهجرة ، وكان فيها غزوة بدر الموعد وغزوة الأحزاب

BIQAI:103:3/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r17.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:103:3/r17.claim: In Biqāʿī's account of Badr, reports of opposing forces and hypocrites nearly frightened the Muslims; the Prophet vowed to go even alone, and 3:173 was revealed.
BIQAI:103:3/r17.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم " والله لأخرجن ، ولو لم يخرج معي أحد "

BIQAI:103:3/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r18.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:103:3/r18.claim: Biqāʿī connects the Confederates' terror, described in 33:10, with the Prophet's declaration after they left: “Now we will campaign against them, and they will not campaign against us.”
BIQAI:103:3/r18.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عند ذهابهم : " الآن نغزوهم ولا يغزوننا "

BIQAI:103:3/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:3/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:3/r19.claim: The four pronouns point to year nine AH and the expedition of Tabuk, the Campaign of Hardship; its patience brought delegations and renewed honor.
BIQAI:103:3/r19.anchor: فإذا ضممت إليها الضمائر الأربعة أشارت إلى سنة تسع ، وقد كانت فيها غزوة تبوك ، وهي غزوة العسرة

DURR:103:1/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:103:1/r2.speaker: أبو مليكة الدارمي
DURR:103:1/r2.claim: Abū Mulayka al-Dārimī, a Companion, says two Companions would not part after meeting until one recited the whole sūra to the other, then they exchanged greetings.
DURR:103:1/r2.anchor: عن أبي مليكة الدارمي- وكانت له صحبة- قال : كان الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:103:1/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:103:1/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:103:1/r5.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr recited the reading attributed to Ibn Masʿūd with the addition “he is in it until the end of time” before the exception.
DURR:103:1/r5.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن عبد الملك قال : سمعت سعيد بن جبير يقرأ قراءة ابن مسعود

DURR:103:1/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:103:1/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR:103:1/r6.claim: Ibrāhīm says they recited the expanded “until the end of time” wording and identifies it as part of ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd’s reading.
DURR:103:1/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال : قرأنا «والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر

IBNASHUR:103:3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r1.claim: The exception completes the warning by dividing people into two groups: those who incur loss and those who escape it.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r1.anchor: فيتقرر الحكم تاماً في نفس السامع مبيناً أن الناس فريقان

IBNASHUR:103:3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r2.claim: Believers who do good avoid loss so long as they do not omit good acts by committing their opposites, sins.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r2.anchor: لا يلحقهم الخسران بحال إذا لم يتركوا شيئاً من الصالحات بارتكاب أضدادها

IBNASHUR:103:3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r3.claim: Repentance is among the greatest good deeds: a believer who avoids sins or repents of them gains the recompensed profit of a good outcome; one who neither does good nor repents remains in loss.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r3.anchor: ومن أكبر الأعمال الصالحات التوبة من الذنوب لمقترفيها

IBNASHUR:103:3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r4.claim: Loss ranges from eternal loss caused by denying God's oneness and the Messenger's truth to lesser degrees measured by outward and inward sins; minor lapses may be forgiven when major sins are avoided.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r4.anchor: فأعظمه وخالده الخسر المنجر عن انتفاء الإيمان بوحدانية الله وصدق الرسول

IBNASHUR:103:3/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r8.claim: The definite plural means the whole class of good deeds, comprehensively including all religiously commanded good acts and abstention from sins.

IBNASHUR:103:3/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r9.claim: The relative clause and its coordination hint at why these people are excepted: faith and good deeds are the opposite of the loss predicated of everyone else.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r9.anchor: مضمون الصلة ومعطوفها إيماء إلى علة حكم الاستثناء

IBNASHUR:103:3/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r10.claim: Faith applies uniformly to its particulars, while good deeds admit degrees; accordingly, freedom from encompassing loss varies with the amount of good done.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r10.anchor: وأما الصالحات فعمومها مقول عليه بالتشكك

IBNASHUR:103:3/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r11.claim: The exception implies that the rest of humanity loses through lacking faith and good action; the relative clause identifies faith and good action as preventing loss from engulfing a person.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r11.anchor: سبب كون بقية الإنسان في خسر هو عدم الإيمان والعمل الصالح

IBNASHUR:103:3/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r12.claim: Exhorting one another to truth is singled out from good deeds for emphasis, since people may wrongly think righteous action benefits only oneself.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r12.anchor: عطف الخاص على العام للاهتمام به لأنه قد يغفل عنه

IBNASHUR:103:3/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r13.claim: Mutual counsel in truth includes teaching guidance and sound beliefs, and training oneself to understand them by doing good and avoiding wrong.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r13.anchor: تعليم حقائق الهدى وعقائد الصواب وإراضة النفس على فهمها

IBNASHUR:103:3/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r14.claim: Patience is also singled out as a particular of good deeds, specifically the endurance required to establish truth and bear harm in doing so.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r14.anchor: والتواصي بالصبر عطف على التواصي بالحق عطف الخاص على العام

IBNASHUR:103:3/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r15.claim: Patience is restraining oneself from a desired thing or its pursuit, either to avoid resulting harm or to gain a benefit; examples include jihad, pilgrimage, and arduous work for reward, wealth, or reputation.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r15.anchor: منع المرء نفسه من تحصيل ما يشتهيه أو من محاولة تحصيله

IBNASHUR:103:3/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r16.claim: Patience includes enduring the displeasure or verbal abuse one may face when enjoining what is right.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r16.anchor: ومن الصبر الصبر على ما يلاقيه المسلم إذا أمر بالمعروف

IBNASHUR:103:3/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r17.claim: Enduring the effort involved in sinful pleasures is not patience, because desire for that effort outweighs aversion to the effort of leaving the sin.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r17.anchor: فليس من الصبر لأن ذلك التحمل منبعث عن رجحان اشتهاء

IBNASHUR:103:3/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r18.claim: These two exhortations encompass the religious good: Islamic beliefs and ethics fall under truth, while good works and avoiding sins fall under patience.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r18.anchor: العقائد الإسلامية والأخلاق الدينية مندرجة في الحق

IBNASHUR:103:3/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r19.claim: Patience underpins the virtues: moral discipline requires resisting many desires until good character becomes a settled trait.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r19.anchor: التخلق بالصبر ملاك فضائل الأخلاق كلها

IBNASHUR:103:3/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r20.claim: Ibn ʿAshur cites ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs's couplet to illustrate giving up beloved food and restraining a wayward heart to avoid lasting disgrace.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r20.anchor: إذا المرء لم يترك طعاماً يحبه

IBNASHUR:103:3/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r21.claim: The cited hadith says Paradise is surrounded by hardships and Hell by desires, supporting the need for self-restraint in righteous action.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r21.anchor: حفت الجنة بالمكاره وحفت النار بالشهوات

IBNASHUR:103:3/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r22.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNASHUR:103:3/r22.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib is quoted as saying that patience is a mount that never stumbles.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r22.anchor: وعن علي بن أبي طالب : « الصبر مطية لا تكبو

IBNASHUR:103:3/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r23.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r23.claim: The author refers to his fuller discussion of patience under the command to seek help through patience and prayer.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r23.anchor: وقد مضى الكلام على الصبر مشبعاً عند قوله تعالى : { استعينوا بالصبر والصلاة }

IBNASHUR:103:3/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r24.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r24.claim: The reciprocal form makes mutual exhortation to truth and patience a constant feature of believers' communal life; it presumes that people practice what they urge others to maintain.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r24.anchor: وأفادت صيغة التواصي بالحق وبالصبر أن يكون شأن حياة المؤمنين قائماً

IBNASHUR:103:3/r25.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r25.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r25.claim: The reciprocal exhortation suggests believers will uphold truth and endure hardship for the interests of Islam and its community, since exhorters ordinarily regard the matter as worth maintaining.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r25.anchor: أن أحداً لا يوصي غيره بملازمة أمر إلا وهو يرى ذلك الأمر خليقاً بالملازمة

IBNASHUR:103:3/r26.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r26.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r26.claim: The assumption that exhorters practice what they urge recalls God's rebuke to Israelites who command goodness while neglecting themselves.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r26.anchor: وقد قال الله تعالى توبيخاً لبني إسرائيل

IBNASHUR:103:3/r27.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r27.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r27.claim: The author connects this point to the earlier discussion of people failing to urge one another to feed the needy.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r27.anchor: وقد تقدم هذا المعنى عند قوله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:103:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r4.claim: Those who spend their lives urging one another to truth and patience and acting accordingly suffer no loss and have gathered all good.
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r4.anchor: ومن كان في مدة عمره في التواصي بالحق والصبر والعمل بحسب الوصاة فلا خسر معه

IBNATIYYA:103:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r7.claim: Ali is also reported to add that mankind remains in loss until the end of time, except those who believe.
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r7.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب أنه قرأ «إن الإنسان لفي خسر وإنه فيه إلى آخر الدهر إلا الذين »

IBNATIYYA:103:2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r9.speaker: سلام أبو المنذر
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r9.claim: Salam Abu al-Mundhir reads al-asr with kasra on ṣād and biṣ-ṣabr with kasra on bā; both are allowed only in pause by transferring the vowel.
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r9.anchor: وقرأ سلام أبو المنذر : «والعصِر » بكسر الصاد ، «وبالصبر » بكسر الباء ، وهذا لا يجوز إلا في الوقف على نقل الحركة

IBNATIYYA:103:2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r10.claim: Abu Amr reads biṣ-ṣabr with kasra on bā and ishmaam; this too occurs only in pause.
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r10.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو : «بالصبِر » بكسر الباء إشماماً ، وهذا أيضاً لا يكون إلا في الوقف

IBNATIYYA:103:3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r4.claim: Those who spend their lives urging one another to truth and patience and acting accordingly suffer no loss and have gathered all good.
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r4.anchor: ومن كان في مدة عمره في التواصي بالحق والصبر والعمل بحسب الوصاة فلا خسر معه

IBNATIYYA:103:3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r7.claim: Ali is also reported to add that mankind remains in loss until the end of time, except those who believe.
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r7.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب أنه قرأ «إن الإنسان لفي خسر وإنه فيه إلى آخر الدهر إلا الذين »

IBNATIYYA:103:3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r9.speaker: سلام أبو المنذر
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r9.claim: Salam Abu al-Mundhir reads al-asr with kasra on ṣād and biṣ-ṣabr with kasra on bā; both are allowed only in pause by transferring the vowel.
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r9.anchor: وقرأ سلام أبو المنذر : «والعصِر » بكسر الصاد ، «وبالصبر » بكسر الباء ، وهذا لا يجوز إلا في الوقف على نقل الحركة

IBNATIYYA:103:3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r10.claim: Abu Amr reads biṣ-ṣabr with kasra on bā and ishmaam; this too occurs only in pause.
IBNATIYYA:103:3/r10.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو : «بالصبِر » بكسر الباء إشماماً ، وهذا أيضاً لا يكون إلا في الوقف

IBNKATHIR:103:1/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:103:1/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:103:1/r2.claim: A report places Amr b. al-As with Musaylima after Muhammad's mission but before Amr's conversion: Musaylima asks what was revealed, Amr recites al-Asr, Musaylima offers nonsense verse, and Amr calls him a liar.
IBNKATHIR:103:1/r2.anchor: ذكروا أن عمرو بن العاص وفد على مسيلمة الكذاب

IBNKATHIR:103:3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:103:3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:103:3/r1.claim: The exception consists of those who believe in their hearts and perform righteous deeds with their limbs.
IBNKATHIR:103:3/r1.anchor: فاستثنى من جنس الإنسان عن الخسران الذين آمنوا بقلوبهم ، وعملوا الصالحات بجوارحهم

IBNKATHIR:103:3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:103:3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:103:3/r2.claim: Mutual counsel in truth means carrying out acts of obedience and leaving prohibited acts.

IBNKATHIR:103:3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:103:3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:103:3/r3.claim: Mutual counsel in patience applies to calamities, decrees, and the harm of those whom believers command to do right and forbid from wrong.
IBNKATHIR:103:3/r3.anchor: على المصائب والأقدار ، وأذى من يؤذي ممن يأمرونه بالمعروف وينهونه عن المنكر

MAWARDI:103:3/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:3/r1.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI:103:3/r1.claim: Yahya b. Sallam says the truth they urge one another to uphold is monotheism.
MAWARDI:103:3/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنه التوحيد ، قاله يحيى بن سلام .

MAWARDI:103:3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:3/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:103:3/r2.claim: Qatada says the truth they urge one another to uphold is the Qurʾan.

MAWARDI:103:3/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:3/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:103:3/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the truth they urge one another to uphold is God.

MAWARDI:103:3/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:3/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:103:3/r4.claim: A further possibility is that people urge their heirs at death to die only as Muslims.
MAWARDI:103:3/r4.anchor: ويحتمل رابعاً : أن يوصي مُخَلَّفيه عند حضور المنية ألا يموتنَّ إلا وهم مسلمون .

MAWARDI:103:3/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:3/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:103:3/r5.claim: Qatada says they urge one another to patience in obeying God.
MAWARDI:103:3/r5.anchor: أحدهما : على طاعة الله ، قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI:103:3/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:3/r6.speaker: هشام بن حسان
MAWARDI:103:3/r6.claim: Hisham b. Hassan says they urge patience in carrying out what God has prescribed.
MAWARDI:103:3/r6.anchor: الثاني : على ما افترض الله ، قاله هشام بن حسان .

MAWARDI:103:3/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:3/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI:103:3/r7.claim: A further interpretation is patience in avoiding forbidden acts and following desires.
MAWARDI:103:3/r7.anchor: ويحتمل تأويلاً ثالثاً : بالصبر عن المحارم واتباع الشهوات .

NASAFI:103:3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:103:3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:103:3/r1.claim: Believers who do good are exceptions: they trade this world for the afterlife, gaining profit and felicity.
NASAFI:103:3/r1.anchor: فإنهم اشتروا الآخرة بالدنيا فربحوا وسعدوا

NASAFI:103:3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:103:3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:103:3/r2.claim: Truth is the established matter that cannot rightly be denied: all good, including God's oneness, obedience, and following His books and messengers.
NASAFI:103:3/r2.anchor: { وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بالحق } بالأمر الثابت الذي لا يسوغ إنكاره

NASAFI:103:3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:103:3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:103:3/r3.claim: They urge one another to avoid sins, obey God, and endure the trials God sends His servants.

NASAFI:103:3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:103:3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:103:3/r4.claim: Both instances of “urge one another” are past-tense verbs coordinated with the preceding past-tense verb.
NASAFI:103:3/r4.anchor: في الموضعين فعل ماضٍ معطوف على ماض قبله

QURTUBI:103:3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:103:3/r1.claim: The exception is from al-insān, which here means people as a whole; this is the sound interpretation.
QURTUBI:103:3/r1.anchor: استثناء من الإنسان ؛   إذ هو بمعنى الناس على الصحيح

QURTUBI:103:3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:103:3/r2.claim: Doing righteous deeds means carrying out the prescribed obligations; Qurṭubī identifies the believers as the Prophet’s Companions.
QURTUBI:103:3/r2.anchor: أي أدوا الفرائض المفترضة عليهم ،   وهم أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI:103:3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:3/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
QURTUBI:103:3/r3.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb asks the Prophet for the sūra’s meaning: the oath is by late day, the human in loss is Abū Jahl, faith is Abū Bakr, righteous deeds ʿUmar, truth ʿUthmān, and patience ʿAlī; Ibn ʿAbbās also preached this as a Companion report.
QURTUBI:103:3/r3.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب : قرأت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم { والعصر } ما تفسيرها يا نبي الله

QURTUBI:103:3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:103:3/r4.claim: Tawāṣaw means loving one another, advising one another, and urging one another on.

QURTUBI:103:3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:3/r5.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI:103:3/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that al-ḥaqq means declaring God’s oneness.
QURTUBI:103:3/r5.anchor: { بالحق } أي بالتوحيد ،   كذا روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI:103:3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:3/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:103:3/r6.claim: Qatāda says al-ḥaqq means the Qurʾān.

QURTUBI:103:3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:3/r7.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI:103:3/r7.claim: Al-Suddī says al-ḥaqq here is God Himself.
QURTUBI:103:3/r7.anchor: وقال السدي : الحق هنا هو الله عز وجل

QURTUBI:103:3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:103:3/r8.claim: Mutual exhortation to patience means patience in obeying God and refraining from disobedience.
QURTUBI:103:3/r8.anchor: على طاعة الله عز وجل ،   والصبر عن معاصيه

RAZI:103:3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r1.speaker: من قال : العمل غير داخل في مسمى الإيمان
RAZI:103:3/r1.claim: Those who exclude deeds from the definition of faith argue that conjunction of faith and righteous deeds would otherwise be redundant; unlike emphatic mention of a class’s noblest member, righteous works are not faith’s noblest subtype.
RAZI:103:3/r1.anchor: احتج من قال : العمل غير داخل في مسمى الإيمان ، بأن الله تعالى عطف عمل الصالحات

RAZI:103:3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r2.speaker: من قال : العمل غير داخل في مسمى الإيمان
RAZI:103:3/r2.claim: They distinguish this verse from cases that single out a particularly honored member after a general category, such as 33:7 and 2:98.
RAZI:103:3/r2.anchor: كقوله تعالى : { وإذا أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح }

RAZI:103:3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r3.speaker: الحليمي
RAZI:103:3/r3.claim: Al-Ḥalīmī accepts repetition here: although faith does not include righteous deeds, the latter include faith and the following mutual exhortation, making the earlier wording dispensable.
RAZI:103:3/r3.anchor: قال الحليمي : هذا التكرير واقع لا محالة ، لأن الإيمان وإن لم يشتمل

RAZI:103:3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r4.speaker: الأولون
RAZI:103:3/r4.claim: The first group replies that repetition for emphasis is possible, but its being possible does not erase the presumption against repetition, which supports their argument.
RAZI:103:3/r4.anchor: إنا لا نمنع ورود التكرير لأجل التأكيد ، لكن الأصل عدمه

RAZI:103:3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r5.speaker: القاطعون بوعيد الفساق
RAZI:103:3/r5.claim: Those who insist the threat against grave sinners is fulfilled argue that only people possessing both faith and righteous deeds escape loss; whoever lacks either faces loss in this world and the next, so the saved are few and fear should be intense.
RAZI:103:3/r5.anchor: احتج القاطعون بوعيد الفساق بهذه الآية ، قالوا : الآية دلت على أن الإنسان

RAZI:103:3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:103:3/r6.claim: The exception consoles believers for lost life and youth: their deeds have brought them something better than those years.
RAZI:103:3/r6.anchor: أنه تسلية للمؤمن من فوت عمره وشبابه

RAZI:103:3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:103:3/r7.claim: Whatever draws a person to obey God is righteousness; whatever distracts from God toward something else is corruption.
RAZI:103:3/r7.anchor: أن كل ما دعاك إلى طاعة الله فهو الصلاح

RAZI:103:3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:103:3/r8.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer from calling deeds righteous that their goodness lies in benefits inherent in them, not merely in a divine command.
RAZI:103:3/r8.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : تسمية الأعمال بالصالحات تنبيه على أن وجه حسنها

RAZI:103:3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r9.speaker: الأشعرية
RAZI:103:3/r9.claim: The Ashʿarites answer that God calls the deeds righteous without specifying whether their goodness comes from inherent benefits or from command.
RAZI:103:3/r9.anchor: وأجابت الأشعرية بأن الله تعالى وصفها بكونها صالحة

RAZI:103:3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:103:3/r10.claim: The verse names the cause of profit but not its outcome, and the outcome of loss but not its cause: loss can arise through sinful action or omitted obedience, whereas profit requires action.
RAZI:103:3/r10.anchor: إن الخسر كما يحصل بالفعل ، وهو الإقدام على المعصية يحصل بالترك

RAZI:103:3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:103:3/r11.claim: Alternatively, the text leaves loss vague but spells out profit, a presentation fitting divine generosity.
RAZI:103:3/r11.anchor: أنه تعالى في جانب الخسر أبهم ولم يفصل ، وفي جانب الربح فصل وبين

RAZI:103:3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:103:3/r12.claim: Because believers love obedience, they do not restrict themselves to personal good works; they urge others to follow the same way and become causes of others’ obedience.
RAZI:103:3/r12.anchor: لا يقتصرون على ما يخصهم بل يوصون غيرهم بمثل طريقتهم

RAZI:103:3/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:103:3/r13.claim: The duty to guide one’s household parallels 66:6; exhortation to truth encompasses the whole religion in knowledge and practice.
RAZI:103:3/r13.anchor: وعلى هذا الوجه قال تعالى : { يا أيها الذين آمنوا قوا أنفسكم وأهليكم نارا }

RAZI:103:3/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:103:3/r14.claim: Exhortation to patience includes making oneself endure the difficulty of duties and avoid prohibitions, since doing disliked things and restraining desired things are both hard.
RAZI:103:3/r14.anchor: والتواصي بالصبر يدخل فيه حمل النفس على مشقة التكليف

RAZI:103:3/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:103:3/r15.claim: Salvation requires all four qualities; alongside personal faith and good works, people owe others calling to religion, sincere counsel, enjoining right, forbidding wrong, and wishing for them what they wish for themselves.
RAZI:103:3/r15.anchor: فدل ذلك على أن النجاة معلقة بمجموع هذه الأمور

RAZI:103:3/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:103:3/r16.claim: The repetition of mutual exhortation assigns one clause to calling people to God and persistence in truth, and the other to enjoining right and forbidding wrong.
RAZI:103:3/r16.anchor: ثم كرر التواصي ليضمن الأول الدعاء إلى الله ، والثاني الثبات عليه

RAZI:103:3/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r17.speaker: عمر
RAZI:103:3/r17.claim: ʿUmar prayed that God show mercy to whoever points out his faults.
RAZI:103:3/r17.anchor: وقال عمر : رحم الله من أهدى إلي عيوبي

RAZI:103:3/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r18.speaker: author
RAZI:103:3/r18.claim: Truth is burdensome and accompanied by trials, which is why it is paired with mutual exhortation.
RAZI:103:3/r18.anchor: دلت الآية على أن الحق ثقيل ، وأن المحن تلازمه

RAZI:103:3/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r19.speaker: author
RAZI:103:3/r19.claim: The past-tense form tawāṣaw praises what they did and signals their desire to persist in it in the future.
RAZI:103:3/r19.anchor: إنما قال : { وتواصوا } ولم يقل : ويتواصون

RAZI:103:3/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:3/r20.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI:103:3/r20.claim: Abū ʿAmr recited bi-l-ṣabr with a slight, incomplete quality on the bāʾ; Abū ʿAlī says this fits a pause, and only rarely a connected reading treated like pause.
RAZI:103:3/r20.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو : { بالصبر } بشم الباء شيئا من الحرف ، لا يشبع
